segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Why is it “A-da-ke-da” last name Glass?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏄᏓᎴᏅ ᏄᏍᏗᏅ ᎲᎥ ᎪᎯᏴᏛ ᏧᏂᎶᏒ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏯᏂᏪᏎᎯ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᎨᏓ ᎤᎸᏒᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᏯᏅᏗ ᏧᏛᏅ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎠᏓᎨᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎪᎯᎩᏴ ᏧᏂᎶᏒᏍᎩᎾ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏕᎦᏙᎥᎢ ᏫᎦᏛᎢ ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: It was different a long time ago, as they came along. “Ah-da-ke-da”, “U-lv-sa-d(i)” you’d think they said, but “A-da-ke-di” was our name a long time ago, as they came along, they said.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏛ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏥᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: Really, that’s what they used to say all the time, wasn’t it?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Where were you born?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏓᎷᏫ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎪᎢ ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏩᏛᏏᏙᎸ
segments.translation: Tahlequah is where I was born, but where I grew up, Greasy is what they call it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎭᎳᎩᏅ ᏱᏣᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᎨᎮ ᏣᎴᏅ ᏕᎭᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᏍᎩᏃᎯᏌ ᏕᏣᏕᎳᏆᎥ
segments.translation: What was your age when you started school? Tell us about going to school.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: You mean at Greasy?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ ᏧᏃᏢᏒ Kentucky ᏧᏙᎩᏓ ᏥᎪᏢᏒ bunch Ꭲ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏗᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏕᎦᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᏃ Ᏺ Ꮲ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ. ᎩᎵᏃ ᎪᎢ ᏧᏩᏮᎴᏅᎲ Ꮓ ᏦᎢᏁ ᏥᏕᏥᏂᏙᎲ ᎩᎵᎾ ᎤᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏩᏂᏯᎥ ᏧᏮᎩᎧᏅ Ꮓ ᏥᎦᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎠᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ
segments.translation: That one they had Kentucky it was called, that’s where I started school, but, I didn’t speak English back then, until I started third grade at Greasy. They put me in where the rest were, and then I started learning how to speak English.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᏓᏱᏍ ᎨᎮ ᏣᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏣᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏣᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: Was it hard for you to learn to speak English?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏱᎦᏅᏛᏗ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏃᏛ ᎤᎴᏅ ᎠᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ. ᏢᎮᏂ Ꮓ ᎡᏝᏪ ᏱᎾᎦᎵᏍᏗᎮ Ꮓ ᏣᏬᎮᎸ
segments.translation: I don’t remember that it was too hard, but then my mom, the late, started learning how to speak English, then it wasn’t quite so hard.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: They spoke all Cherokee, didn’t they?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏙᎯᏳ Ꮫ Ꭵ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᎵᏌ ᎠᎩᏚᏓ Ꮕ ᎬᎦᏛᎯᏍᏛᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏐᏁᎵ ᏯᏩᏕᎢᏴᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏥᏚᏂᏢᏅ. ᎾᎮᏂ ᏂᏗᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᎩᎶ ᎮᏂ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏁᎲ ᏢᏅ ᏧᎾᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏱᏚᏂᎮ ᎢᎦᏗ ᎲᏍᎫ ᏗᎦᏚᎴᎾ ᏱᏚᏂᎮ. ᏍᎩᎾᏅ Ꮩ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᎠᏲᏁᎦ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᎸᏢᏅ ᏧᎾᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎠᏯᎥ ᎤᎾᏣᎷᏘᏍᏛᏅ. ᎤᎾᏅ ᎠᏥᎴ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, my grandma and grandpa are the ones that raised me then. I was nine years old when they filed the papers. The reason was, a long time ago, people didn’t have a telephone and some didn’t have an automobile. My dad was white, and somewhere he was in a bar that had an explosion, and he got killed.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᏭᏅᏃ ᎩᎶᏅ ᏴᏫ ᎤᎾᏛᎦᏁ ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᎤᏂᎷᏤ ᎡᏥ ᎡᏙᏗᏅ ᏥᎨᏥᏃᏎᎴ. ᏍᏛᎦᏎᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᏍᎫᎾ ᎩᎶ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᏯᏂᏯᏅᎰᎦ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎤᏙᏕ ᎠᏥᎷᎦ ᎨᎪᎮᎴᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎮ you know ᎤᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᎢᏁᏒᎢ ᎠᎪᎮᎴᏅ Ꮎ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏫᏗᏂᏢᏅᎢ ᏢᎮᏂ ᎤᏲᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏩᏓᏅᏘ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏁᏙᎲᎾ ᏱᎦ ᎢᎦᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᏳ Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᎩᎶ ᎩᏂᏴᏅᎡᏗ ᎠᎪᎮᎴᏅ Ꮎ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.translation: Then someone heard about that, and they came and told my mom to watch out, there might be some whites coming to get the little girl, because her dad got killed, they said. That’s when my late mom got frightened. “Let’s go to town,” she told the old man. “Let’s file papers. I would feel bad all the time if she wasn’t around. I love her a lot, and I don’t want someone else to take her away from us,” she told the old man.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏃ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏚᏂᏢᏁ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎩᎶ ᎠᎨᏯ ᎤᏴᏟᏢ ᏗᏘᏲᎯᎭ ᏗᏯᎥ ᏭᏴᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᏂᏙᎲ ᏧᏬᏚ ᏗᎵᏲ ᏓᏩᎵᏲᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏬᏚ ᎠᏌᏃ ᎠᏩᏒᏃᎲ ᎩᎶᏅ Ꮎ ᏴᏫ ᎤᎾᏛᎦᏂ ᎠᏕᎳ Ꮕ ᏕᎨᏥᏁᎴ ᏗᎬᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨ. Ꮂ..ᎠᏩᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏧᎾᏓᎯᎵᏓᏍᏗ ᎢᏤᏓ sdᎢ ᎨᎲ. ᎯᎢᏅ ᏕᏍᏗᏩᏒ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏧᏄᏬᎢ ᎨᎪᎮᎴᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏬᏚ ᏗᎾᏬ ᏕᎬᎩᏅᏁᎸ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᏂᏙᎲ ᎠᏩᎦᏎᏗᏕᎬ Ꮎ mike ᎥᎩᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏄᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ
segments.translation: They filed the papers, that I remember. Then, some woman came in, she went in to an attorney’s office, and she was in there a long time. I remember that I was playing around. I had on real pretty socks and I had on a pretty dress. Some people heard about that and gave my parents money. “You have to go to the courthouse, so buy clothes for this little girl to wear,” they were told. Then they got me real pretty clothes. As I was playing around, he was watching Mike, my brother, that’s what I remember happened then.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᎧᏲ Ꮲ ᎠᎸᎯ ᎠᎦᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: For real, I never heard that.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Uh-huh, uh-huh.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏅᏃ ᏭᏂᏍᏆᏕ Ꮓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏂᏓᏅᏁᎲ Ꮓ?
segments.translation: That’s when they finished filing the papers then?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏢᏅ ᎥᎸᎯᏳ ᎥᏩᏝᏃᎮᏛᏅ ᏱᎦ ᏙᏳ ᎠᎩᏥ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏚᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏪᏥ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎤᏥ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎨᏯ Ꮲ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᏝᏃᎮᏛᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ. ᏍᎫ ᎾᎾ ᏳᎷᏤ ᎣᏤᏙᎲ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎬᏬᏏ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᏅᏢ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏙᏟᎩ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎤᏁᎳᎩ ᏍᎩ ᎤᏲᎱᏌ ᎠᏩᏓᏙᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ “ᎠᏩᏁᏢᏅ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏚᏰᏟᏕᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᏴᏂᎮᏍᏗ ᏓᎨᏏ ᏁᎳᎩ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᏚᎵᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᏗ ᎤᏁᎳᎦ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏛᎩᏃᏎᎸᏂ” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ ᎦᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗᎲ “ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᏁᎳᏅ ᎾᎩᏴᏅᏓ ᎨᎮᏍᏓ Ꮲ ᏱᏓᎨᏌ Ꮭ ᎠᏮᏌ ᎨᏒ ᏱᏓᎨᏏ ᏍᎫ ᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᎨᎡᏍᏗ ᏢᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎠᎩᏔᏲᏢ ᏱᎦ ᏥᎨᎢ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏩᏁᎳᏅᎯ. ᏢᏅ ᎲᎸᎯᏳ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᏗᏬᎮᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎤᎶᏐᏅ
segments.translation: My real mother never spoke to me. My late grandfather, she was his daughter, but she had a different mother. And that woman never had spoken to me. Even if she came close to us, she wouldn’t say a word to me, so we didn’t know each other when she died. One time I prayed, “My Lord, if for some reason she calls for me, I’m going. If there’s something she wants to tell me, it will be up to her if she wants to tell me something,” I said to him, praying. “But God, if she doesn’t call for me, I’m not going. Not for myself, I’m not going. Let it be that way with my life, I didn’t ask for my living,” I told my God. She never said anything to me, that’s the way it went.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: She lived close by?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, Stillwell ᏛᏅ ᎤᏴᏢ ᏗᏝ ᎸᏢ ᏥᏓᏰᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, she lived someplace the north side of Stilwell.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᎧᏲ, Ꮎ ᏥᏃᎮ Ꮎ Kentucky school Ꮮ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏄᏰᏟᏛ ᎠᏯ ᏂᏙᎦᏕᎳᏆᎥᎾ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ. ᎠᏬᎯᏳᎲᎾ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎤᏂᏍᏚᏅ ᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᎠᏯ ᎣᎦᎴᏅᎯ ᏂᏅ ᏥᏃᎮ ᎤᎾ ᏕᏣᏕᎳᏆᎡ
segments.translation: Really! I don’t know the Kentucky School that you’re talking about. We didn’t go to school there. I believe it was shut down by the time we started school, but you went there to school.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏔᎵ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏱᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎸᏢ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏁᎮ ᏓᎷᏩ ᎠᏁᎯ ᏣᏂᎷᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎲᏍᎫ ᏱᏗᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏧᎾᏙᎩᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏗᏓᏟᎶᏍᏛᏅ ᏓᎩᎭ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏤᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏯ ᏯᏪᎾ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏃᏢᏅᏍᎩ ᏣᎦᏔᎾᎥ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏬᏢᏗ Ꮎ ᏗᏯᏟᏗ ᏥᏓᏃᏢᏅᏍᎩ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏣᎦᏔᎭ ᏧᏬᏢᏗ ᏗᏯᏟᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Ꮎ ᏗᏰᎦᏟ ᏱᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏂᎦᏭ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏣᏃᏢᏅᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᏣᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏅᏛᏁᎲ
segments.translation: I don’t know if I went two years of school there. Some used to come from somewhere like Tahlequah. I don’t remember their names, but I’ve got pictures. My late mom, she would go, too, when I went. They would make something, and she knew how to make things like necklaces. She knew how to make things like that, and quilts, too, stuff like that. They would make anything. While we were in school, that’s what they would be doing.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏝᏅᏲ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮎ ᏗᎾᏕᏲᎲᏍᎦ
segments.translation: The teachers there, didn’t they speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᏂᎦᏗᏭ ᎾᏛ Ꮲ ᏱᎦᏅᏛᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ Ꮎ ᎩᎶ ᏤᏙᎲ ... Cowan ᎨᎵ ᏧᏭᏛ
segments.translation: No, none of them. That one whose name I don’t remember, she would come. Cowan, I think, was her last name.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Agnes?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: That’s it, I think.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏤᏙᎲ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᏥᏓᏃᏪᎵᏍᎬ ᏏᏅ ᏓᎩᎾ ᎡᏥ ᏧᏂᏙᎸ ᎪᏪᎳ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ bus Ꭲ ᎮᏂ ᏥᏙᎩᏴᏅᎰᎯᎲ. ᎤᎾᏅ ᏦᏤᏛᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏙᏣᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᎠᏯ ᏦᏥᏲᏟ ᏁᎸᎩᏅ ᏧᎾᏛᎾ ᎤᏅᏌ ᏣᎾᏕᎳᏆᎥᎲᏍᎬ ᎤᏃᏢᏅᏗ
segments.translation: She would come there, and they would write in Cherokee. Still, Mom had the papers I got, and they would learn it. The bus would come and get us, and that’s where we would be. We used to have schooling, us kids, and the adults would be learning how to make things.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮂ, ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏥᏥᏯᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏄᏌ. ᏙᎲ ᎤᏰᏟᏛ ᎠᏯ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏙᎦᏕᎳᏆᎥᏂ ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎲ. ᏗᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᎤᏂᏍᏚᎮ ᏛᎮ ᎦᏳᎳ ᏣᏬᎮᎲ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᏂᎯᏅ ᎤᎾ ᏕᏣᏕᎳᏆᎡ
segments.translation: That’s what I was asking my dad a while back. “How come we didn’t go to school there?” I said. “I don’t know, maybe it was already shut down, but you went there to school.”

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ ᎤᏟᏗᏢ ᎮᏂ ᏣᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏂ Williams
segments.translation: Yeah, the Williams lived alongside it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, Cecil?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: No, that.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Arthur?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, Arthur!

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏥᎦᎷᎬ. ᎾᏅ ᎠᏦᎸᏂ ᏱᏗᎦᏘ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏔᏂ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: That boy used to come and look in the window. He was a big boy.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: John.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ “ᏧᏫᎭᏂᎦ” ᏣᏃᎮᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏥᏯᏙᎵᎬ ᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏅᎮ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏛᏁᏗ ᎤᏚᎵᎮ. ᏃᎴ ᏴᎦᎶ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏯᏂᎦ ᏃᎴ ᏙᏯ ᏱᏙᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙ ᏴᎦᎷᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏓᏅᏘᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: “Just go on home,” they would tell him. I felt sorry for him. He wanted something to do. He’d walk by and go home, then when we played outside, he came again. He used to be real friendly.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He wanted to join what you all were doing.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, he used to wear overalls all the time.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎯᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏄᏛᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎸᏢ ᏱᎦᏙᎦ
segments.translation: He would be standing somewhere, like this [gestures].

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ. ᏓᏁᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏩᏂᎷᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏯᏴᏟᎦ ᎾᏅ ᎤᏅᏗ ᎣᎩᏢ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏳᏩᏗᏓ
segments.translation: He was like that all the time. He would come to our house. He’d come in and he’d drink all of the milk we had. That’s what he would do inside, drink it. He was real friendly. I felt sorry for him.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᏛᎰᏂ ᏍᎫᏅ. ᏓᏁᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏪᏓᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏩᏓᏘᎾᎢ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎤᏴᏟᏢ “Bye, Corehead!” ᏥᏩᏗᎲ ᎮᏂ “Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏓ ᎲᏗ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Bye, Corehead! ᏫᏥᏲᎮᏅ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏙᎨ? ᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏂᏪᏍᎨᏍᏗ!” – “ᏍᎩᏗᎰᏂ ᏂᏍᎩᏪᏎᎮᏍᏗ ᏓᏩᏙᎥᎢ ᏔᎵᏁ ᎢᏍᎩᎪᎲᎢ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᏗᎰᏂ” ᏣᏗᎲ...”ᎤᏫ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ. ᏳᏓᎭ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏱᏙᎧᏃᎩᏍᏗ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎾᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ Johnny Cash ᏧᏃᎩᏓ ᏱᏙᎧᏃᎩᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: I did, too. He would come to our house, too. I already had kids, and the girl came in. “Bye, Corehead!” she said. “What are you saying?” I said to her. “‘Bye, Corehead,’ I’m saying to him,” she said. “Why? Don’t be saying that!” I told her. “‘Call me that for my name next time you see me’ he told me,” she said. “Ooh-wee!” I said to her. Sometimes he would be playing music. He would sing Johnny Cash songs.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᎾᏂᏪᏎᎲ ᏳᏓᎭ Johnny Cash ᏣᏃᎮᎲ ᎯᏲᎵᎩᏍ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.translation: That’s what they’d call him sometimes, Johnny Cash. Did you know him?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎦᏥᎩᎥᎡ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮂ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎦ ᎨᎲ Arthur Williams ᏥᏲᎵᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: I’ve seen him, but I didn’t know him. Arthur William’s the only one I knew.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: How many kids do you have?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Two.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: How old are they?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᏛᏃ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏅᎩᏍᎪᎯ ᏔᎵ ᏳᏕᏘᏳᏓ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ Lucian ᏚᏙ ᏣᎳᎩᏅ ᎬᏗᏃ ᏙᏧ ᏚᏙ
segments.translation: The boy is going to be 42, Lucian is his name, and in Cherokee his name is “Toh-juh-wi”.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: The girl?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: What’s her name in English?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Lucian.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Lucian Warrior ᏚᏙ. ᎾᏅ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ Ꮓ ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᏌᏭ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ Ꮓ Whitney ᏚᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ Whitney Warrior ᏚᏙ well ᎦᏁᎵᏛ DeerinwaterᎮᏂ ᏭᏗ Ꮓ
segments.translation: Her name is Lucian Warrior. Her girl will be now 21. Her name is Whitney Warrior. Well, she’s married now. Deerinwater is her last name now.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏧᎾᏍᏗᏭ Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ. ᎠᎾᏁᏦᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎭᏓᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏥᎾᏅᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᎾᏁᏦᏍᎬ. Ꭰ ᎾᎾ ᏨᏛᏏᏙᎲ Ꭰ ᎦᏝᏛᏅᏍᎩᏍ ᎨᎮ ᏣᎵᏌ ᏣᏥ Ꮥ
segments.translation: They were little ones when I saw them. Them boys used to play ball. They done well playing ball. Did your mom do any canning when you were growing up?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, just about anything.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Plant it, did she?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏫᏒᏍᎬ ᎡᏧᎳ. ᏃᎴ ᎦᏰᏫᏒᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏥ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏓᏕᏲᏂᏙᎲ ᏧᏌᏃᏍᏗ ᏥᏓᎪᏢᎾᏁᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Oleta ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎥᏛᏁ ᎨᎲ. ᎪᎨ ᎮᏂ ᏱᎦ ᏥᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏙᏯ ᎤᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏧᏃᏚᏨ ᏥᏚᏰᎲᏍᏛ. ᏃᎴ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᏯᏑᏂᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏃᎴ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎦᏝᏓᏅᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎪᎵ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏓᏂ Ꮓ ᏗᏰᎦᏟᏛ ᎦᏰᏮᏒᏒᎬᏂ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᎦᏃᎭᎵᏙᎯ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᏂ ᏌᎶᎵ ᏱᏙᎦᏃᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᏱᎬᏩᏛᏗ ᏥᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏓ ᏥᏓᏍᎷᏍᎬ
segments.translation: They planted a lot, and she did sewing. She would make your late mom’s dresses for her when she was teaching. She would be doing something all the time. In the spring, she’d work outside. She planted very beautiful flowers, and she would fish down at the creek. She canned things when winter came. Sewing quilts sometimes, too. My late mom would go hunting, and sometimes she would bring home squirrels. Anything a man can do, she done. She would split wood, too. That’s what she would do.
She really was doing that, wasn’t she?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: She was tough, wasn’t she?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s the way they were back then, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᏗᏓᏅᏫᏍᎦ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏅᏓᏗ ᎠᏎ ᏍᎫ Diane ᏯᏅᏛᏗ ᏗᏓᏅᏫᏍᎦ. ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏣᎩᏍᏗᎬ ᎮᏂ ᏢᏂ ᎦᎾᎦᏗ ᎨᏙᎯ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᎫ ᏂᎦ ᏚᎴᏣ ᏥᏛᎩᎳᎡᎸ. ᏃᎴ ᎪᎵ ᎡᎯ ᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ Ꮲ ᎩᎶ ᏗᎦᏚᎴᏂ ᏳᎮ ᎡᎳᏗᏭᏅ ᏦᎩᏁᏅᏒ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᏅᎾ ᎠᏁᏟᏗ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᎩᎾᏫᏗ ᎠᏕᎳᎰᏍᎨ ᏓᎩᏴᏪᎬ ᏦᎩᏂᏎᎦᏍᏛᏅ ᎩᎶ ᎠᏓᏟᎲ ᏗᎩᎾᏗᏅᏍᏛᏅ ᎾᎯᏳᏅ ᏮᎩᏓᏅ ᏧᏂᏢᎩ ᎪᎵ ᎡᎯ ᏯᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎯ
segments.translation: My late dad, he was a healer. I remember that, too. Dianna probably remembers, he was a healer on anything. When I was little, I didn’t go to a doctor, only when my tonsils were taken out. Then I had pneumonia one time. I remember no one had a car there, so we went on foot with my late dad, and he’d try to carry me at times. He knew I was tired. We got lucky. Someone was driving by and picked us up, then put me in the hospital.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Stilwell or what?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, Ꮎ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏣᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏥᏥᏯᎥ ᎾᏅ ᏒᎾᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ ᏛᎮᏢ ᎠᎩᏴᏞ. ᎠᏎᎠᎾ ᏍᎩᏱᎦ Ᏺ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏪᏙᎳ ᎦᎾᎦᏘ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏩᏏ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏯᎸᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᎦᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏴᏩ ᎠᏂᎷᎦ ᏓᏍᏕᎵᎲ. ᏃᎴ ᏒᏃᏯ ᏯᏂᎷᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.translation: Yeah, I was in that old building. And I was in about a week. That’s all I remember about going to the doctor. And, too, himself, he would look for things to help us, and he would help people that came, and they used to come at midnight.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎦᏅᏛᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏧᏂᎷᏨ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᎠᏁᎯ “‘ᏥᎩᎵ Ꮕ ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏄᏁᏁᎮ ᎬᏮᏁᏦᏎᏛ ᎢᏣᏢᏅᏢᏭᏅ ᎤᏅᏳᏍᎬ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᎦᏙ ᏯᎾᎵᏒᎯ ᎨᎮ” ᏂᎨᏥᏪᎮᎴ ᎮᏂ. ᎤᎾᏚᎵᎮ ᎮᏂ ᎡᏍᎦ ᏳᎾᏓᏛᏗ ᎠᏎᎾ “ᎯᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏥᏥᎦᏛᎾ” ᏥᎨᎪᎮᎸ “ᎠᏩᏁᏢᏅ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᏁᎸ ᏣᏩᏅᏔᎾ ᏞᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏲ ᏱᎬᏓ ᏱᎦ ᎩᎶ. ᎤᏅᏏ ᎮᏂ ᏛᎤᎾᏨᎡᎵ ᏢᏴ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮲ ᏯᎾᏘᏴ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎢᏣᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗᏭ. ᎤᏩᏏ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏅᏑᏭ ᏭᏓᎤᏂᎷᏤᎵ” ᏥᎨᎪᎮᎸ
segments.translation: One time I remember old women came from Old Belfonte. They were being bothered really bad. “Your family is jealous of something,” he told them. “I don’t know if they were fighting over land,” he told them, because they wanted to fight back. “But this stuff, I know,” he told them. “God gave them to me, the things I know. People are not supposed to do bad to anyone, it’s going to come back on themselves someday, they just don’t know when. But just pray about it, it’s going to come back on them,” he told them.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏩᎾᏔ ᎠᎩᏚᏓ ᎤᏁᎫᏧᏓ ᏁᎨᏒᎾ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᎠᏎᎾ Ᏺ ᎠᏩᎾᏔ ᎮᏂ Ᏺ ᎠᎦᏔᎾᎡ. ᏥᎪᎥ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ. ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᎷᎬ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎯᎾ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᎦᎷᎬ ᎠᏲᏁᎦ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ. “Is Mr. Glass home?” ᏯᏓ ᎮᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ “Ꭽ!” ᏯᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎦᏳᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏅᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏓᏰᏙᎵᏒ. ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏕ ᏙᏯ ᎨᏙᎲ ᎾᏅᎾ ᎠᏓ ᏧᏍᎷᏍᏗ ᎤᏬᏢᎮ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏕᎦᏒᏛ ᎠᏓ. ᏌᏭᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᏩᏅ ᎤᎵᏍᏛᏡᏍᏗ ᏱᏚᏍᏓᏰᏌ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏬᏞ ᏳᏓᎭ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏛᎩᏴᏢ ᏥᎪᎥᎾ ᏧᏬᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏛᏠᎸ ᎩᎶᏭ ᏩᎩᏴᏢ ᎩᎶᏭ ᏩᎩᏴᏢ ᎤᏛᏠᎸ Ꮎ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ “Is Mr. Glass home?” ᏛᏳᏛᏅ ᎯᎢ ᎾᏮᏛᏁᎸ Ꭶ ᎩᎶᏭᏅ ᏥᏛᏥᏴᎯ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ. ᏢᏅ ᎸᏢ ᏳᏬᏞ ᏢᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏟᏍᏓ ᏳᎬᏩᏓᎾᏫᏍᏛᏂ, ᎤᏗᏍᎦᏢᏁ ᎮᏂ
segments.translation: That’s when I knew my late grandpa wasn’t mean, but I know that he knew things, I’d seen him. Sometimes white people would come. This one man would come - he was white. “Is Mr. Glass home?” he would say. “Haw!” he would say. He’d already know that guy was coming. One time I was outside where he had a spot for splitting wood. There was a stack of wood he had for when he got tired. He would sit on there sometimes. Then I came out and I saw him sitting there. He drove up. I’d just went in and he drove up, that old man. “Is Mr. Glass home?” he said. I turned, wondering. “I just came in the house,” I thought, “and already he wasn’t sitting out there.” He couldn’t have run that quick. He had just hid.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Disappeared.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏃᏭᏅ Ꮓ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ Ꮓ ᏄᏪᏌ “ᏣᏅᏗᏍᏅ ᏥᏗᎦᎵᎦ Ꭸ?” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ. “Ꭵ,” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᎴᎾᏁ ᎦᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛᏂ ᏍᎫ Ꮎ ᏗᎾᏢᏗᏍᎦ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏙᎬ ᎦᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛ ᎠᎾᏢᏗᏍᎬ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎮᏂ. ᎠᏩᏛ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏩᏛᏁᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏢᎮᏂ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏎᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, and this one time he said, “You know that wildfire way over yonder?” he said to Mom. “Yeah,” my mom said. “I set that fire, and I was watching the firefighters. I was standing there watching them putting out the fire,” he said. I knew he could do that. He wasn’t mean, but…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He knew things.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎠᎦᏔᏁᎡ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᎦᏔᏁᎢ ᎨᎲ ᎢᎦ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏌᎹᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏂᏗᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎡᎶ ᏣᎦᏎᏍᏙᏗ ᎨᎰ ᎾᏍᎫ ᏥᏓᏓᏁᏟᏴ ᎪᎵ ᎪᎨᎡ ᏃᏭ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨ ᎯᏍᎪᎵ ᏱᏤᎯᏍᏓᏁ ᏧᏛᏅ ᏄᏕᎴ ᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏙ ᎪᎵ ᏱᎦ ᎪᎩ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎯᏍᎪᎵ ᏱᏤᎯᏍᏓᏁ. ᏄᏓᎴ ᎮᏂ ᏅᏫᏘ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᏤᎯᏍᏓᏁ ᎡᎰ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏧᏛᏅ ᎾᎮᏅ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᏥᏄᎾᏛᏂ ᏴᏫ ᏂᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏩᏂᏍᎪᏐᏂ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎲᎮᏂ ᏍᎩ ᏯᏛᏗ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏎᎮᏂ ᎠᎯᏯᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎪᎵ ᏱᎦ ᎯᏍᎪᎵ ᏱᏤᎯᏍᏓᏁ ᏗᏩᏛᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᏅᏬᏗ ᏣᏙᏗ. ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎪᎩ ᏱᎦ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᎩᏐᎲᏍᎪ ᎢᎾ ᏢᏅ ᎣᏏ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏱᏣᎵᏘᏏ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏂᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎬᏩᎦᏓ
segments.translation: He knew things, really. He knew a lot of things. He was really smart. He knew the reason you have to watch for everything in this world, including the changes of winter and spring. “Right now, you have a headache,” he said. “It is different in winter, spring, or summer. If you have a headache, there is a specific kind of medicine for your headache. The medicine exists at the time you have a headache,” he said. Nowadays, these people would dig up all of the medicine, and you shouldn’t do that. You have to leave some. But if it’s winter and you have a headache, you’re going to find the medicine to use. And, too, if it’s summer, others will get all of it, and that’s not good. And, too, it will get away from you, it will move for good.

segments.text: ᎠᎵᏒᎲᏍᎪ ᏛᎮ ᏙᎭ Ꮎ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏧᏩᏂᎩᏍᎪ
segments.translation: All of it runs out when they get all of it.

segments.translation: Yeah, some chant and some pray and, too, the moon phases at times water it empties out, and you’re fixing tobacco when it’s thundering. When it thunders and someone is working it hard, thunder makes a good time to fix it.
It’s been a long time since I heard that.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Ꮎ ᏯᎾᎬᎵ ᏍᎫ Ꮓ ᏯᎾᎦᎵ ᏛᏲᏃ ᎤᏁᏘᏍᏓ Ꮓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏗᎦᎸᏫᏍᏓᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏈᏍᏓ ᏣᎦᏍᎪ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎬᏅᎦᎵᏍᎪ ᏳᏓᎭᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏱᏣᎵᏏᏛᏂ Ꮎ ᎠᎹ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏣᎦᏍᎪ.
segments.translation: And lightning, too. When lightning gets bad, it’s a good time to work like that. And heavy rain, too, it cleans all away, and sometimes if you save that water, it, too, is medicine, that rain.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎡᏥ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏕᎬᎩᎶᏍᏗᎲ ᏍᏗᎩᏗ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᎣᏩᏌ ᎠᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎤᏅᏥ ᏱᎦ ᎯᏍᎪᎵ ᏱᎦ ᏱᏤᎯᏍᏓᏁ ᎪᎵ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎫᏅ ᎤᏅᏥ ᏱᏣᎵᏏᏛᏂ ᏍᎫᏅ ᏱᏝᎲᎦ ᎯᏍᎪᎳ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏱᎦᏅᏒᏁᏐᏂ ᎩᎶᏩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏱᎬᎾᏬᏐᏂ ᏃᎴ ᎤᏗᏝᎦ ᏱᎦ. ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏅᏱ, ᏅᏱ ᏱᏗᏣᏩᏛᎯ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᎾᎤᏂ ᎤᏂᏒᏙᏟ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᏱᏗᏣᏩᏛ ᏱᏗᏣᏢᏂᏭ ᎠᏴᏝᏗᏍᏙᏗ ᏍᎫᏅ ᎯᏍᎪᎵ ᏱᏤᎯᏍᏓᏁ ᏙᏅᏍᎫ Ꮎ ᏌᏭ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᎤᎵᏌ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪᏒ ᏥᏰᏲᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ.
segments.translation: My late mom, that’s what she used to wash clothes, kind of like for your own help, they say. And snow, too. If you have a headache, if you save that snow in winter, and you have a headache, put all of it on your head. Pull it out, it will melt away quickly and then it will be hot again. And rocks, too. If you find some that are kind of slender in a creek bed, you put them in the freezer for your headache. Really, one of my sister’s grandkids was amazed when I taught her that.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᎴᏒ Ꭱ Ꮎ ᏅᏱ ᏙᏅ ᎤᏝᏅ. “Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏓ ᎲᏛᏁ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏁᏟᏗᎮᏅ ᎠᎩᎪᎲ Ꮕ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎲ. “ᎦᎵ ᎾᏂ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᎤᏗᏝᎨ Ꭿ ᏅᏱ ..ᎥᎲ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏂᎦᏗ Ꮫ ᎦᎾᏎᏁᏐᏂ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏴᏫ ᏙᎨᏥᏰᏠᎰ. ᏃᏭᏅ ᏦᎢᎦ Ꮽ ᎦᏳᎳᏛ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᏗᎾᏛᏁᎸᎲᏍᎩ, ᎤᏂᏅᏍᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ “ᎩᎵ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᏣᏗᏫᏌ ᎩᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎦᎨᏓ ᏗᏣᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᏗ” ᏯᎾᏓᏙᏏ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏅᏱ ᏕᎬᎩᎳᎡᎸ ᎡᏥ Ꮕ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏬᏢᎾᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᏮᎵᎬ ᏍᎫ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏚᏙᎥ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏯᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏩᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎠᏬᏢᎾᏁᎸ “ᎯᎢᎾ ᎭᏗᏔᎲᎢ ᏦᎢ ᎢᎦ ᏳᏓᎭᏭ ᎭᏗᏔᏍᎨᏍᏗ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᎭᏫᏂ ᎮᏂ ᏢᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏯᏓᏅᏫᏍᎪ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏙᏯ ᏗᏝ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏓᎠᏅᏩᏅ ᏱᎦ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎠᏎᎾ ᎭᏫᎾ ᏲᏝ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎠᎬᏱ ᎮᏂ ᎣᎾᏗᏝ, ᏙᏯᏗᏝ ᏓᏣᏗᏫᏏ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎩᎵ Ꮓ ᎭᏫᏂ ᎩᎵ Ꮓ ᏣᏗᏫᏍᎪ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎯᎾ ᎯᏅᎵᏰᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏍᏗ Ꭰ ᏧᏙᏛᏮᏓ ᏍᏗᎦᎭᏭ ᎭᏗᏔᏍᎨᏍᏗ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᏃᏭᏅ ᏦᎢᎡᏁᎢᎦ ᏧᎵᎪᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ. ᏍᎩᏅ ᎾᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒᏂᏭ ᎠᏩᏗᏩᏒ
segments.translation: She got that rock out and put it on her head. “What are you doing?” I said. She was trying it out because she had seen me do that. “Golly, Na-n(a), this rock is hot!” she said. “Yeah, it pulled all of it out,” I told her. And at times, when people have surgery, and just after three days they would be out doing something, they were against that. “You need to wait until you’re healed to do hard work,” they would tell you. One time, I had taken out stones, and my mom made me medicine. I can’t recall what it was called, that she looked for, and she made me this drink. “Drink it for three days, just anytime drink it,” she said. “Deep inside don’t heal itself, but outside may heal itself good. But inside it hasn’t,” she said. “First the outside is going to heal up, then later the inside will heal up,” she said. “So take this daily, drink a little at a time, and after three days it will be good,” she said to me, without realizing it healed up.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎠᎩᏳᏆᏗᎲ, ᎠᎩᏳᏆᏗᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏅᏩᏅ. ᏍᎩᎾ Ᏺ ᎠᏥᎳ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏰᏒᏛ ᏂᎬᏁᎰᏛ ᎠᎵᏥᏍᏉ ᎯᎢ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎾᏮᏁᎸ Ꭶ ᎡᎯᏍᏓ ᏛᏲ ᎠᏪᎯᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏏᎾ ᎯᎢ ᏅᎬᏁᎲ ᏍᏓᏯ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎪᎯᏴ ᎠᎩᏑᎶᎯᏍᎡᎸ ᎪᎯᏗ Ꭱ ᏙᎯ ᎠᏪᏙᎸ. ᎦᎾᎦᏘᎾ ᏱᏚᏂᎪᎵᏰ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏧᎾᏓᏅᏕᏍᏗ. “ᏙᏅ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎯᎾ ᏥᎾᏙᎩ ᎫᏍᏕ ᎤᎵᏎᎦ ᏄᏍᏓ?” ᏱᎬᏬᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ. Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ Ꮟ… ᎯᎩᏍᎪᎯ ᎯᏍᎩ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ Ꮭ ᎭᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᏦᏎᏛᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎩᎵ Ꮎ ᏖᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎩᎾᏕᏍᏓ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾᎾᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎮᏂ ᎣᎾᏗᏢ ᎬᎩᎾᏕᏍᎨ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏅᏗᎲ ᎤᏃᎰᏎᎴ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏩᏂᏍᏛᏁ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎭᏫᎾᏴ ᏭᎵᏍᏆᎵᏐᏁ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏎ ᎤᏂᎾᏌᏁᏍᏓ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ
segments.translation: Then, one time I had a toothache that my dad the late treated. He used hot coals in his palm, and spit in it with his finger going round and round. Right here he put it [gestures], golly, painful it was hurting, too. He did like this hard [gestures], but in a little while the pain went away. I was pain-free a long time. When the doctors looked at it at the dentist, “What’s on your tooth? Something weird is on your tooth,” they’d say to me. I don’t know, but for 55 years, that tooth never even bothered me until just recently, I had to have it pulled out. They were pulling out this back tooth, and they dropped the tool they were using, and it hit that tooth, and it broke off way deep. Then they had to pull it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That long it helped you?
