segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He really knew a lot, though, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏙᏳᏛᏲ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏍᎫ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎮᎾ ᏩᏩᏂᏏᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏕᎦᏝᏗᎲ ᎲᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏚᏯ ᏱᎦ ᏱᏗᎦᏝᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏝ Ꮩ ᎠᏍᏚᏓ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏛᏳᏴᏢ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏚᎴᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏍᏓᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏃᏴᎵᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎣᎩᏅᏏᏭᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᏭᏴᏢ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏗᎤᏅᎪᏨ ᏫᏅᎪᏨ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎾᏗᏝ ᏩᎩᏅᎪᏨ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏫᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛ ᎤᎵᏏᎬ ᏫᏥᏙᎬ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎤᎾᏅ Ꮎ ᏙᏯᏗᏝ ᏫᎬᏙᎬ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏭᎦᏎᏍᏛ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎦᏛᎩᏍᎬ ᎩᏟ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏂᎨᎯᏙᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏍᎩᏃ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏗᎤᏴᏝ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏣᎦᏎᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᏦᎢ ᏭᏢ ᏳᏒᎯᏓ ᎫᏍᏕ ᏓᏅᏛᎦᏂ ᎾᎡ ᎠᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᎤᏢᎨᏍᏗ ᏓᏅᏛᎦᏂ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᏙᏅ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᏂᏙᎲ ᏙᏯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏚᏣ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ George ᎤᎾᎾ ᎤᏓᏝᏫᏍᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎫ ᎤᎷᏨ ᎡᎵᏭᏏ ᏱᎦᏍᏕᎳ ᎵᏓ Ꭱ ᎤᏢᎩ ᎤᏬᏗᏐᏅᎢ ᎤᏄᎸᎲᏍᎩ ᎤᎭᏬᎵᏕᏍᏗ ᎠᎪᎮᎸ ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏓᏩᏛᏒ ᏙᏅ ᎦᏂᏟᏅ ᎠᏴ Ꮎ ᎦᏍᎩᎶ ᎤᏂᏝ ᎤᏂᏢ ᎤᎾᏅ ᎤᏬᏢ ᎤᏄᎸᏅ ᎤᎭᏬᎵᏕᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏚᏴᏅᎲᏒ Ꮎ ᏧᏂᏢᎦ ᏗᎦᏂᏙ ᎤᎷᏨ ᎤᎾᏘᎾᏫᏛᎲ Stilwell ᎤᏅᏗᏅᏒ. ᏍᎩᏃ ᎵᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ Marble CityᏛ ᏰᎲ ᎤᎷᏨ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎢᎤᎷᏥ ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᎹᎹ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎦᏛᏓᏍᏗ ᎪᎵᎬ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᏒᎮ ᏒᎾᎴ ᏥᎨ ᏫᎳ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᎵᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ ᏫᎳ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎾᎬᏁᎲ ᎤᏌᏃ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ you know ᎣᏍᏓ ᎾᎬᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᎵᏍᏛᎢᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎯᎡ ᏄᏩᏁᎳ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎯᎡ ᏱᎩᏓ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᏂᏴᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾᏅ Ꮎ ᎩᏟ ᎤᏂᏂᏴᎮ ᏍᎩᎾᏅᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, really. And one time, I had already gone to bed and my mom was canning. I don’t know if it was beans she was canning, but she told me later, “Something came in the front door,” she said. And my late dad got up, she said. “I noticed a real loud noise, and it was just us two,” she said. “That thing went in one room, and then came out, and then it went outside,” she said. “Then, afterwards, I went out the back. And I was standing in the dark, watching it,” she said. “There, outside, it was standing there looking at something,” she said. “I could hear the dogs chasing something.” Then, when she came back in, he said, “You watch. In one day we’re going to hear something,” he told her. “That old woman is going to be sick, we’ll hear,” he told her. So, I was playing outside, and my uncle, the late George, he was staying there, too. He came up [and said], “Can you help me? Li-d(i) is sick. She’s swollen all over, and she can’t breathe,” he said to the late U-da-sa-d(a). Then, I went along, and on the bed they had that chair, and she was sitting on it. She couldn’t breathe. Then, my dad went to get the ambulance, and it came. They took her to Stilwell. Then, the late Lid(i)’s sister, who lived in Marble City, she came. Whenever he came, Da-sa-d(a) the late, he’d tell Mom, -- I’d listen all the time, and I understood what they would talk about,-- Yesterday morning, that Wi-d(i), that Lid(i)’s late sister Wi-d(i), she was fixing her dress. “Where it had come open,” she said. “When she did this [gestures],” she said, “there was a spot this [gestures] big where something had grabbed her,” she said. “That’s where the dogs had got her.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s who they were after outside.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎦᏛᏛᏅ ᎵᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎵᏓ ᏙᏅ ᎤᏍᏗᎾ ᏣᎵᏍᏓᏁᎳ ᎠᎭᏂ?” -- “ᎾᏛᏅ ᏧᏂᏢᎦ ᎤᎾᏦᏙᏗ ᎬᎩᏯᏍᎬ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎬᎩᎾᏏᏂᏙᎲ” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏢᏅ ᎬᏩᎵᏟᏗᏟᏗᏭ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎤᏬᏘᏍᎣᏅ ᏧᏔᏂ ᎨᎮ ᏗᎦᏅᏍᎨᏂ ᏂᎬ ᏎᎦᏨᏭᏅ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ “ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᎩᏝ ᎬᏩᏂᏴᎮ” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: They had asked her, “Lid, what happened to you here?” – “It was the ambulance drivers putting me in, they pulled me around roughly,” she said. She couldn’t even move her legs were swollen all over. They were big, and she could just barely speak. “Because the dogs had got me,” she said.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: “Lid” is that the one lived close?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, that old woman.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What was her husband’s name ?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: “De-wi”.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He was small, wasn’t he? With round glasses and big--

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏧᎭᎨᏓ ᏧᎦᏘᏅᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꭵ. ᏍᎩᏛᏅ ᎩᏟ ᎮᏂ ᎬᏩᏂᏴᎲ. ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏞᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏚᎸᏩᎦᏕ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ. ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏫᏥᏩᏛᎯᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏮᏌ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏛ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᎾᏅ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏯᏁᏙᎲ Ꮲ ᏱᏚᎸᏉᏕ ᎾᏍᎫ ᏦᎨᏅᎲ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏁᎫᏣ ᎾᎴ ᏱᎦ ᏦᏍᏛᏓᎸ ᎤᏪᏣ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏳᏁᎫᏣ ᏱᏓᏮᏁ ᏃᏭᏛᏲ ᏯᏥᏃᎷᎦ ᎨᎲ. ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎦᏟᎲ ᎤᏅᏏᏴ ᎠᎬᏯ ᏗᏢᎾ ᏗᏝ ᎣᏥᏯᎥ ᏥᏓᏳᏪᏡᏅᎡ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏬᎩᏴᏢ “Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ?” ᎣᏦᎮᎸ Chris. Chris ᎮᏅ ᏚᏙ “ᎾᎢ, Ꮎ, ᎾᎢ…” ᎤᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎤᏬᏂᎯ[ᏍᏗ] ᎵᏗ Ꮕ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᏁᎫᏕᎮ
segments.translation: Yeah, he had on real thick glasses, yeah. That’s who the dogs had got. She was mean, that old woman - she didn’t like kids. Sometimes I would go visit her, I was the only one she liked, that old woman, and if the kids were there, she didn’t like them. And at home, if someone was into meanness, or my sister’s boy was mean or hitting me, she would come after him. One time, he was asleep in the corner. We were in the front room when he started screaming. So we went in. “What is it?” we said to Chris. Chris is his name. “That--that--that,” he couldn’t talk. The late Lidi was bothering him.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Ooh-we!

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏩᎦᏎᏍᏗᏕᎬ. ᏳᏓᎭᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏧᏂᏢᎩ ᏱᏫᎦᎾᎩ ᎨᎲ. ᎠᏗᏝ ᎮᏃ ᏥᏭᏂᎶᏒ ᏥᏭᎾᏁᎸᏛ Florene ᏦᏍᏛᏓᎸ, ᏍᎩᎾ “ᎤᎾ ᏩᏠᏒᎢ Ꮓ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ Ꮓ ᎢᏨᏠᏒᎢ” ᏱᎬᏬᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏅᏃ ᏧᏂᏢᎩ ᏫᎦᎾᎬᎢ “ᎤᎾᏭᏅ ᏱᏪᏙᎢ” ᎬᏬᎮᎸ Ꮲ ᏯᎩᎸᏉᏕ ᎤᎾ ᏩᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏓᏤᏢᏂᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏰᎸᏒ. ᏍᎩᏃ ᎠᏩᏣᎥ Ꮓ ᎣᎦᏂᎩᏏᏗᏒ ᎾᎠ ᏦᎩᏰᎵᏒ “Ꮭ ᏱᏓᎦᏠᏏ ᎠᎭᏂ” ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏛᎦᏂᎩᏌᏭ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏮᏏ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏮᏌᏭ ᏫᏓᏥᎷᏣ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ. ᎤᎾ ᎠᏩᏣᏩᏗᏒ bus Ꭲ ᏩᎩᎷᏥᏅ Ꮓ ᏩᎩᏴᏟᏢ ᏍᏗᎩᏗᏅ ᏥᏍᎦᏱᎲ . ᏥᏍᎦᏱᎲᎮᏂ ᎠᏩᎾᏛ ᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᎵᏓ ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᏩᏪᏙᎸ aunt lidi ᎮᏂ ᏥᏲᎮᎯ ᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏭᏏ ᏱᎬᏒᏏ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ? Ꭵ, ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᏳᏫᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏤᏓᏍᏗ ᎬᏲᏎᎰᎢᎾ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ. ᏗᎾᏬᏅ ᏓᎩᏁᏒᏒ ᎠᎩᎷᏥ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏒᏃᏱ ᎯᎠᏗᏝ ᏩᏮᎦᏛ ᎾᏅᏅ ᎠᏁᎦᏍᏛ ᏗᏝ ᏩᏮᎦᏛ ᎠᎩᏰᏨᎡ ᏒᏃᏯ ᎠᏩᎾᏛᎡ ᏂᎦᏂᎬᎾ ᎨᎲ ᎦᏕᎳᎣᏍᎬᎡ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬᎡ ᏗᏩᏟᏆᏗᏅᏗ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏒᎾᎴ Ꭱ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎤᏗᏛᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᏅᏛ Ꮎ ᎠᏮᏌ ᏥᏂᎬ ᎤᎵᏨᏙᏩᏓ. ᎸᏢ ᏅᎮ ᏪᏙᎮ ᏥᎵᎲ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ
segments.translation: That’s the way she was. I always was watching. Sometimes my mom would be in the hospital. They went somewhere else, and my sister moved in. Then, “Get off there, after school,” they’d tell me, because my mom was in the hospital. “You should be there,” they told me. I didn’t like to go there all the time. I just didn’t feel right. There I was on the bus, and we were ready to go home after school. “I’m not going to get out here,” I thought. “I’m just going home, even if I’m by myself at home,” I thought, as I was riding on the bus. When I got there, I went in. I was a little scared. I was scared because I knew the way things were at that time. Then I went to Lid’s house. “Aunt Liddy,” I used to call her. “Can I spend the night with you?” I said. “Yeah,” she told me, “I told you, you can come anytime,” she told me. I went to get my clothes. Then I came back about midnight. I was facing this [gestures] way, towards the wall. I woke up at midnight, and I knew she wasn’t in bed. I could tell, but I couldn’t turn over. Then, real early in the morning, she was already up. I knew I was alone in bed all night. I guess she went way off while I was asleep.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: She was boogering somewhere, wasn’t she?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎥᎲ, ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎴᏱᎦ “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᏫᏴᎯᎮᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎤᏒᏛ ᏥᏗᏓᏁᎵ” ᏯᏬᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏲᏢ ᏱᏩᏩᎦᏔᏁ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏅᎮ ᎦᎾᏰᎦ ᎤᏱᏗ ᏴᎨᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ “ᏣᎦᏎᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏝ ᎮᏙᎲᎢ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ Ꭱ ᎠᏂᎶᏍᎪ ᎤᎾ” ᏯᏬᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸᏅᎡ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏃᎴ ᏱᏛᎦᏅᏂ ᎦᏚ ᏧᏓᏞᏍᎬ ᎦᏐᏩᎸ ᏥᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᎠᏩᎦᏎᏍᏛᏅ ᏱᏫᏚᏗᎾ *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏫᎾᏮᏛᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏞᏍᏕ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎡᎳᏓ ᏳᏙᎦᎦᏥᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎢᎦ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᎦᏔᎾᎢ ᎨᎲ ᏗᏩᏛᏒ. ᎦᏥᎦᏎᏍᏛ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᏍᎫ ᏳᏓᎭᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏴᎬᏃᎮᏢᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎪ ... ᎾᏛ Ꮎ ᏢᎮᏂ ᏙᏳ ᏱᎦ ... ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᏂᏃᎲᎳ ᏥᎨᎲ. “ᎮᏍᏓ ᏴᏃᏒᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎤᎵᏏᏂ” ᏯᎾᏓᏙᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᏯᏅᏓᏕᎰᏗᏭ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᏩᏛᏃ. ᎾᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎵ “Ꭽ!” ᏯᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏓᎭ Ꭰ ᎯᎢ Ꮫ ᏥᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏱᏥᏲᎮᎳ. Mama said if you take care of it. It will last longer ᏱᏓᏴᏬᏏ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏟ ᏂᏗᎦᏪᏍᎪ
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s the way she was sometimes. “Don’t be going in that building,” she’d tell me. It was behind the house. I didn’t look back there, ’cause I thought it might be something scary. Then, “Watch it when you’re over here. The little people come by here,” she’d tell me. She told me things all the time. Then, when it was going to rain, she would go get the bread and roll it round. I was watching when she threw it. She’d do this [gestures], and it would never hit the ground. She knew a lot of things. As I was growing up, I observed. Then, too, she talked about things, too. And, my late dad would talk about things, too. Then sometimes, they would talk about things that are not real. And then, “Don’t be sweeping after dark,” they’d say. But, nowadays, they will just laugh at you and make you feel embarrassed. I don’t say anything anymore. Sometimes, my husband will say, “Haw!” When I tell him, “This is what Mom used to say,” he’ll say, “Mama said, if you take care of it, it’ll last longer.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s what he tells you?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Yeah, ᏥᏃᏎᎸᏁᎲᏭ ᎮᏂ “*ᎯᎢ* Ꮫ ᏥᏄᏍᏓ *ᎯᎢ* Ꮫ Ꮭ ᏴᏛᏁᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏃᎴ Ꮎ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏥᏅᏩᎶ ᎮᏍᏓ ᏱᏅᏩᎶᏍᎨᏍᏗ” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ. ᎩᎶ ᎡᏍ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏂᏓᎦᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᏥᏲᏎᎰ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏂᏪᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᎩ ᏴᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏥᏪᏎᎸᏁᎰ ᏱᎾᏛᏴᎩᏪᏌ “Ꭽ..Mama said if you take care of it. It will last longer ᏱᏓᏴᏬᏏ ᎮᏂ
segments.translation: Yeah, I was just telling him things. “*This* is how it was or you don’t do *this*.” And, at night, if you’re hammering, don’t do that. Someone is going to pass on,” I tell him. That’s what they used to say a long time ago. If I tell him that, he’d say to me, “Haw! Mama said, if you take care of it, it’ll last longer.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏣᏕᎰᏗᎰ Ꮫ ᏙᏳ ... ᎫᏍᏗᏍ ᏗᏣᏓᏛᏂ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎵᏗ ᏕᏫᏅ?
segments.translation: Were you kin to Li-di and De-wi?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏕᏫ Ꮎ ᏅᎾ ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏥ ᏳᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎵᏗ ᎢᎾ ᎤᏙᏓ ᏳᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᎾᏢᏅᏢ ᎨᎮ
segments.translation: Yeah, that Da-sv-di late, his mom, and Liddy’s late dad were siblings.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ marble city ᏂᏙᏗᏳᎾᏛᏒ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ. ᎤᏂᎪᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏣᏁᎲ ᎲᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏔᎵᏚ ᏱᎾᏂ ᎨᎮ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᏧᏠᎩ ᏧᏚᏣ ᎤᎾᏗᏝ ᎠᏂ livers Ꭲ
segments.translation: Marble City, where they grew up, a lot were from that family. I don’t know if there were 12 in all, Da-sad’s aunts and uncles from the Livers.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, that’s who they were.
Oh, yeah, it was the Livers.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᏂᎪᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏁᎯ ᎠᏂ double head ᎠᏂ bunch Ꭰ ᎠᏮᎨᏫᏛ ᎠᏂ Sawney ᎤᏂᎪᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏁᎯ ᏂᎦᏗᏅ ᏭᏅᎦᏛ Cherry Tree ᏓᏂᏁᎳ. ᎢᎦᏗᏅ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏗᎾᏓᏛᏂ ᏓᏂᏁᎵ ᏧᎾᏓᏴᏅᏗ
segments.translation: There are a lot of them. Doubleheas, Bunch’s, and I forget Sawneys, there’s a lot in that family and all the rest live at Cherry Tree. Some of them kinfolks are living together.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏂᎦᏩ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎠᎭᏂᏭ ᏥᏓᏂᏁᎳ ᎫᏍᏓᏭ ᎮᏂ ᏗᎾᏓᏛᏂ Ꭰ ᏥᏚᎾᏓᏴᏅᎲ” ᏯᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ
segments.translation: They’re living here, just kinfolks that started living together, is what he’d say, Da-sa-da the late.
Still, they say that.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎪᎯᎩᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏅᏌ ᏥᏓᏂᏍᎪᏍᎪ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏲᎱᏌ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏯᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎫ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎸᏢ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏱᏗᎦᎶᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎹ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏪᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮟ ᏫᏄᎷᏨᏂᏭ ᏓᏁᎸ. ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏏ ᏱᎦ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏱᏛᎦᏂᏙ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏱᏛᎦᏂᏙ Ꮲ ᎤᏂᏅᏍᏛᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎤᏁᏓᏍᏗ ᏓᎾᏓᏍᏆᏂᎪᏗᎲᏭ ᎴᏍᎫ ᎤᏂᏅᏍᏛ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏧᎾᏘᏂᏓᏍᏗ and Ꭰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏒᏃ ᎮᏂ ᏴᎦᎷᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎹ Ꮕ ᎤᏪᏙᎸ ᎨᎮ. ᎤᏅᏖᏅ ᏱᏭᎷᏥ ᎠᏯ ᏗᏬᏢ ᎥᎩᎨᏳ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Then, too, along time ago, they would dig the grave themselves when someone passed away. That’s what he would do, too. He would come walking, and he would go get water before he came to the house. It’s not good to carry around kids or babies. They were strictly against little kids being around the cemetery, or when having a funeral. They were against taking kids. And, at midnight, he would come home. He’d been to the water, and he knew when he came to where I was. He loved me a lot.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏳᏛ, ...Ꮲ ᏯᏅᏛᏗ Ꮎ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏫᏥᎷᏨ ᎦᏳᎵᏍ ᎠᏂᏁᎴ ᎵᏗ ᎤᎾ
segments.translation: Do you remember when you all moved there, was Lid(i) already living there?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᏍᎩᏛᏅ ᎣᎩᏁᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏑᏟᎶᏓ ᎦᏙᎯ.
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s who had given us one acre of land.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏍᎩᏅᏅ ᎣᏣᎦᏎᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏰᎸᎯ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᎬᏴᎳᎬ ᎮᏂ ᎵᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏕᏫ ᎨᎲ Ᏺ ᎦᏳᎳ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ
segments.translation: They meant for us to watch her, because she was getting old, that Lid(i), but Dave the late, he passed on then.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He went first, didn’t he?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎾᏛᏲ ᎦᏂᏰᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏫᎦᏅᏅ Ꮎ ᏥᏗᏥᏁᎵ
segments.translation: That road was scary back then. Down that road where you all lived.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, for real.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ‘ᏥᎩᎵ ᎡᎯ Ꭴ ᏦᏥᏍᎦᏱᎲᏛᏲ ᎤᎾ ᏬᎩᎶᎯᏍᏗ
segments.translation: They always said there was a booger that lived down there. We were scared to go by there.
Marlene, it was. [laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Marlene was sticking up.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᏗᎰᏂ ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎪ Ꮎ ᎭᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᏥᏗᎨᏥᎢᎸᏍᏛᏁ ᎤᎾᎮᏂ ᎤᏂᎶᏒ ᎨᎮ ᎾᎮᏅ ᎾᎥ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎤᏂᏲᎮ ᎤᎾᎮᏂ ᎸᏢ ᏥᎦᏅᏂ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᎤᏣᏪᏐᎸᏍᏕ ᎤᎵᏘᏓ ᎤᎾᏅᏅ ᎤᏂᏩᏛᎮ ᎤᎾᏭᏅ ᎠᏥᎴ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎦᏁᏰᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎡᎯ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ
segments.translation: They’d say, a long time ago, when they force-marched the Cherokees, that’s where they came through, and someone was looking for them. Somewhere along that road, they say, this runaway was resting. They found him there, and he was killed. That’s why something dangerous lives there, they say.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: For sure, there is.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏧᏪᏘ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᏂᏚᏍᏓ ᏕᎦᏂᏌ ᎤᎾ. ᎾᎮᏅ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᏕᏫ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏗᏝ ᏧᎶᏎ ᏒᏃᏱ ᎤᏛᎩᏓ ᏅᎨᎮ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᎤᏍᎦᏎᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ “Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏥᏍᎦᎢᎯ ᏱᎦ” ᎠᏗᏍᎪ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ. ᎤᎾᎡ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏚᎶᏕᏍᏛᏁ ᏣᏗᏍᎬ ᎤᎵᏨᏚᏩᏗ Ꭱ ᎤᎾᏟᎴ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏒᎾᎴᏅ ᎠᎩᏰᏥᏢ ᎤᎾ ᎡᏏ ᏥᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎾᏅ ᎠᎬᏛᎦᏂ ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏒᎾ ᏏᏆ ᏛᏯᎢᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏙᏃ ᎠᏩᎴᏫᏍᏛᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏫᏓᏩᎧᏅᏂ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏍᎦᏰ ᎤᎬᏕ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏃᏭᏅᏃ ᏢᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂᏙᎸ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ Ꮓ ᎣᎩᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᏅ ᎠᎩᎯᏍᏛᏁ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎠᎩᏰᏥᏃ ᏌᎾᎴ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Mike ᏨᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏗᏤᏅ ᏓᏥᏅᏁᎴ ᏧᎳᏑᎶ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏍᎩᏅ ᎣᎾᏗᏝ ᏍᎫ ᏧᎶᏎ ᎾᎥᏂᎨᏍᏗᏅ ᎤᏂᏰᎸ ᏭᏂᎷᎯᏍᏗ ᏓᏁᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏧᎶᏎ ᏍᎫ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᎨᎲᏎ ᏗᏤᏅ ᏧᎳᏑᏟ ᏭᎶᏎ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏗᏤ ᏓᏩᎳᏒᏢ ᎤᎾ ᎠᎹ ᏩᏮᏕᎵᏨ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᎨᎯᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: And there are old graves there. One time, they say Dave, when he was young, came through there around midnight, and he had been drinking, they say. And he was brave. “I’m not scared of anything!” he’d say all the time. There, something tripped him, he said. All night he fought with it, he said. “When morning came, I was still laying there,” he said. “Then I heard something. I thought a hog was coming,” he said, “so I stopped and looked good. That hog had a man’s face,” he said. “I don’t know how it happened, but that’s when I started fighting with it,” he said. “I guess it knocked me out,” he said. “When I woke up, it was morning,” he said. And, Mike was telling, too, that he was given new shoes. He came that way, too, closer toward the house, he said. So he came that way, and then something chased him. He came through the creek with his new shoes on, he said. [laughter] “With new shoes on, I went in the creek,” he said. “Something was chasing me,” he said.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎪ Ꮫ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏂᎪᏩᏘᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏑᏎ ᏣᎾᏗᎲ ᏒᏃ ᎤᎾ ᎠᎹᏯ Ꮎ ᏥᎦᏁ. ᏏᏍ ᎦᏁ ᎠᎹ ᎤᎾ ᏢᎨ Ᏺ
segments.translation: They’ve been saying that they saw something there. Someone was wading there in the creek at midnight. Is there still water there or not?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏳᏓᎭᏅ, ᎢᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎠᏂᎷᎪ ᎡᏍᎦᏂ ᎸᏢ ᏂᏙᏛᏳᏂᎶᏒ ᎤᏲᏟ Ꮫ ᏄᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Umm, sometimes it is really different now. Them whites nearby, it is really bad where they’re from, now.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Can’t get to it now?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: No, not on that old road.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᏬᏚ ᏛᏲ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᎦ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᏒ ᏱᎦ Ᏺ
segments.translation: It was pretty to go through there in the daytime, but at nighttime…

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Where’s that?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: There at Bunch.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Starr Killer Hollow.
Cave Springs. Toward Bunch, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true. She can describe it.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮂ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏛᏴᎦᎶ ᎪᎢ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᎾᎠ ᏗᏝ ᏴᏮᎬᏅᎪᏫᏍᏓ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: I don’t know what its name is. You can come through that way and go by Greasy School, and then you can go out that way, can’t you?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꭵ, Ꮎ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎾᎠ Ᏻ Earnest Johnson ᏣᏂᏁᎸ ᎪᎯᎩᏴ
segments.translation: Yeah, that church close to where Earnest Johnson lived a long time ago.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎲᏍᎫ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ, Ꮂ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᎭᏢ ᎦᏁᎸ ᎾᎯᏳ Ꭰ
segments.translation: I don’t know where he lived back then.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Greasy church-Ꭲ ᎮᏂ ᏙᎭ? ᎤᎾ ᏱᏫᎬᏅᎪᏩ
segments.translation: Greasy, by the church, ain’t it? There, where you can come out.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: That community building they have.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᎾᎾ ᏱᏣᎶᏐᏂ. ᏣᏅᏘᏍ Ꮎ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏥᎪᏢ? Ꭰ Greasy?
segments.translation: Just past that, you know that church they have there at Greasy? Uhh…
South Greasy.
South Greasy.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Yeah, Ꮎ ᏱᏣᎶᏐᏂ ᏱᏣᏕᏲᎵ ᏥᎪᏢ Ꮎ community building Ꮎ ᏣᏒᏟ ᎤᎾ ᏱᏗᏣᎶᏏ ᎤᎾᏭ Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏔᎵᏁ ᏣᏞᏍᏗ ᎤᎾᏭᏛ ᏱᏫᎶ
segments.translation: Yeah, just past that, and around that community building - that bridge over it, there’s the second turn-off. You can go there.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Oh, OK.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: You can go there. Well, you used to be able to.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: In the woods, not now.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᏅᏅ star killer ᏥᎦᏅᎾ ᎤᎾ ᏱᏘᏅᎪᏍᏗ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ Star Killer ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᎤᏚᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏎᎦᏨᏭᏅ ᎠᎮ ᏔᎵ ᏑᏟᎶᏓ ᎠᎯ ᎦᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ Star Killer ᎤᏤᎵ ᏳᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏂᎬᏛ ᏓᏂᏁᎵ
segments.translation: And you can come out on that Starr Killer road, that Starr Killer was Mom’s grandpa, just barely two acres of it is left. It used to be his, that Starr Killer, but whites live all over it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: All around?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They’re buying, too, ain’t it? All of it.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᏁ, ᎮᏍᏗᏂ ᏍᎫ ᎤᎾᏓᏗ ᏱᎦ. ᏙᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᎩᏟ ᏱᏚᏩᏐᏌ ᏣᎲ ᎦᏙ ᏱᏓᏰᏥᏲ ᎮᏂ Ᏺ
segments.translation: They’re not friendly either. If your dog even crosses the property line, it will get shot.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛᏅ ᏣᏂᏁᎳ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎡᎳᏗᏝ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ Star Killer Lake ᎤᎨᏳᏐ, Ꮭ ᎩᎶ Ꮓ ᏱᏫᎬᏴᎭ. ᎤᎾᏅ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎣᎦᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎦᏛᏒ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎯᏭ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏄᏒ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ Ꮎ Pat, Pat Hunter ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎦ ᏛᎮᏃ ᎤᏟ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏂᎬ ᏂᏚᏩᏃ “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏑᎲᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎥᎬᏯ ᏗᏢ ᏗᏪᏅᏒ”
segments.translation: The ones that live there, my dad’s way, they’re stingy with it Starr Killer Lake. Nobody can go in there anymore. We would go swimming there all the time, but just recently he passed away, that Pat. Pat Hunter. His wife will probably be worse. She says, “Don’t be fishing in front of my house.”

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎪᎯᎦ ᎮᏂ ᎬᎩᎶᏒ Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎰ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏗᏝ ᏩᎩᎶᎯᏍᏗ
segments.translation: A long time since I been that way, I don’t want to go that way.

segments.text: ᎤᎾᏍ Ꮲ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎪᏢ ᏗᎦᏣᏄᎳ ᎤᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᏗᎦᎾᏗᏫᏏ?
segments.translation: Isn’t there a cemetery in that area?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, ‘that’ way.
I went there the other day.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You went there?

segments.text: ᏕᏥᎪᎵᏰᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏚᎾᏙᎥ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎦᏓ, ᏫᏛᎨᏙᎵ ᏅᏍᎫ
segments.translation: I was looking at the names. [I thought it was] amazing. I’ll go back again.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᎾᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᎤᏔᎾ ᎥᏓᎵ ᏥᎪᏢ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᎨᏓᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏬᎦᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎤᎾᎮᏂ ᎨᎮ ᏥᎬᏲᏎᎲ Ꮎ Mink ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᏥᏓᏰᏥᎢᎲ ᎾᎠᏂᎨᏍᏗ ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎸᏉᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ--
segments.translation: There, that big pond there, we all used to go there and swim there, too. That’s where I was telling you about, that Mink man that got killed nearby. The late

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: -d(i), really liked--
Her late uncle.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: --ᎤᏑᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎠ Ꮲ ᎮᏂ ᏫᎦᏅᎪᎦ Ꮎ ᎠᎹ ᎤᎾᏅ ᎢᎦ ᎤᎸᏉᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏑᏗ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓᏅ ᎠᏑᎲᏍᎬ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏃᏩ ᎮᏃ ᎤᎵᏏᎲᏍᎦ ᎠᎴᏂ ᎦᏕᎳᎣᏍᎬᏃ ᎠᏂᏑᎵᎪᎬ ᎠᏣᏗ ᎠᏂᏂᏱᏍᎬ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ Ꮕ ᏅᏱ ᏙᏗᏳᏕᎬ Ꮓ ᎪᎯᏴ Ꮓ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏅ Ꮓ ᎠᎹᏳᏟ ᎨᏴ ᎸᏢ Ꮎ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏥᏕᎲ ᏙᏩᎴᎳ ᎪᎯᎩᏴ Ꮎ ᏐᏈᎳ ᏗᎦᎾᏏᏁᏍᎦ ᏍᎩᎡ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏕᎦᏐᎨ ᎠᎹᏯ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎤᎾᏭᏛ ᏍᎫᏃ ᎠᎩᏟᏌᎾ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᏛᎥᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎫᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏂᎪᏩᏛᏗ ᎨᎮ ᎤᎾ ᏂᎪᎸ
segments.translation: --fishing there close, someplace that water goes out, that’s where he liked to fish, he said. One time, he was fishing there, he said. And it was starting to get dark, he said. “I noticed the fish were quitting biting,” he said. Something was tossing rocks, he said. “After a while, then I heard something a ways away in the water--you know, a long time ago there used to be wagons--that’s what it was crossing the creek,” he said. “That’s when I gathered all my stuff and left,” he said. [laughter] But, they used to see something there all the time.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s where my grandma used to live.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏗᎩᏗ ᎣᎾᏗᏝ ᏳᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Yeah, there, a little behind it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏣᏂᎦᏩᏘᎲ ᎫᏍᏓ. ᏂᎪᎸ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏓᏛᏬᏍᎬ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: They used to see something there all the time. We’d swim there all the time, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: But it was good then.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮲ ᎩᎶ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏳᏦᏎᏗᏕᎨ ᎣᏍᏗᏭ ᏙᎯᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Ꮎ ᎵᏗ ᏥᏥᏃᎮᏍᎬ ... ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎯ ᎨᎲ. “ᏗᎦᏚᎲᎡ ᏕᎨᏌ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏍᎩᎪᎲᎾ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏝ ᏙᏯ ᎠᏬᏢ ᎢᎯᎷᏨᏭ” ᏍᎩᏅ ᎣᏥᎶᏍᎬ Ꮎ bus ᏫᎬᏩᏠᏗᎲ “ᏱᏍᎩᎪᎢ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎠᏬᏢ ᏗᎯᎦᏐᏍᎨᏍᏗᏭ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏓᎩᏅᏗᏁᏌ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏯ, Kay, ᏱᏕᎩᎾᏗᏄᎦ” ᏍᎩᏅ ᏳᏍᏗᏭᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏁᎰ ᎨᎰ ᎠᎩᎩᏍᏗ ᏱᎦ ᎧᎵᏤᏣ pop ᎴᏱᎦ ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᎠᎩᏁᎲ
segments.translation: No one was bothered by anything. It was good, and it was just peaceful. Then, too, what I was talking about: All the time, she would tell me, “I’m going to town after a while. When you see me here outside, sitting, come back then.” We would just go by in the bus, and it dropped me off. “If you see me sitting here, come on down to town. She’s going to take us, that woman Kay, she’ll take us.” She would give me something to eat like candy or pop. Anything I wanted, she would give me.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏃ ᏦᎩᏰᎵᏌ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᎣᏣᎢᏒ ᏥᎪᎥᏅ ᎵᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏬᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏩᏮᏠᏒ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏫᏓᎩᏢᏅ ᏃᏭᏛ Ꮓ ᏛᎩᏅᎪᏨ “Hey, hey, hey!” ᎥᏬᎮᎸ “ᎭᏢ ᎮᎦ?” ᏛᏬᎮᎸ Mike “ᎵᏗ Ꮕ ᏧᏪᏅᎲ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Ꮂ! Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏳᏰᏟᏓ ᎤᎾ ᏰᎦ!” “Ꮲ ᎠᏎ ᏂᎯ ᎬᏯᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᏱᎦ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎬᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏩᏛᏁᏓ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Hey, Mom!” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ. “ᎾᎡ Marlene ᎵᏗ Ꭱ ᎡᎦ!”—“Hey! Ꮭ ᎤᎾ ᏱᎦᎮᏂ!” ᎠᏬᎮᎵ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ. “ᏙᎨ ᏂᎪᎸᏅ ᏫᎨᏙᎰ, ᏙᎨ ᏥᏍᎩᏅᏫᏍᏗ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. “ᏒᎾᎴ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏲᎱᏎ!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ. “ᎲᎥ!” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎪᎯᏕ ᎣᎩᎯᎵᏙᎸ ᎬᎩᏃᏎᎲ “Ꮲ ᏰᎭ!” – “Ꮭ! ᏧᏬᏢ ᏥᏓᏥᎶᎢ ᎠᏩᎾᏔ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏓᏲᏍᏕᏏ!” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎪᎯᏗ Ꮫ ᎬᎩᏍᏗᏰᏛᏅ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏁᎨᎲᏂ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ
segments.translation: Then, after school, we were walking, and I saw Lid(i) the late, sitting. So, I got off and put my books down, then I came out. “Hey, hey, hey, where you going?” Mike said to me. “Lid(i)’s house,” I said. “Huh! No use you going over there,” he said. “I don’t have to listen to you,” I told him. “Whatever I think, I can do,” I told him. “Hey, Mom, Marlene is going to Lid(i)’s house!” – “Hey you can’t go there,” said my mom, the late. “How come? I go over there all the time! How come you’re telling me not to go?” I said to her. “She died this morning,” she said to me. “Huh-uh!” I said. It took them a long time to convince me that she had died. “No! She was home when I came by. I know! Because we’re going to town,” I said. It took a long time, them telling me not to go, when she passed on.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᏭᏅ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Arkansas ᎸᏢ ᏥᏩᎵᏍᏕᎵᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏥᏔᎦ ᏧᏂᏴᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᏓᏂᏅᎦᎵᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏬᏥᏯᏅᎲ ᏗᎣᏣᎢᏒ ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒ Ꮫ ᏧᎦᎾᏂᏢ ᏍᎩᏅᎾ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏣᏓᏁᎸ Roberts Funeral Home-Ꭲ ᎤᎾ ᎣᎦᎴᏫᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᏯᏅ ᏦᏥᏲᏟ ᎣᎦᏣᎥᏭ ᏗᎦᏚᎴᏃᎢ ᏧᎾᏔᏂᏅ ᏭᏂᏴᏢ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎣᎩᎷᏣ ᏃᏭᏃ ᎤᏝᎦᎵᏴᏓ ᏃᏭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᏅ ᎡᏚᏣ ᏥᎨᎲ George ᏙᎢᏢ ᎣᏥᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎤᏬᏢ ᎠᏬᏢ ᎯᏄᏍᏓ ᎡᎳᏗ ᎪᎯᏴᏃ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᏥᎴ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏓ ᏛᏳᏕᏲᎸ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏥᏭᏴᏢ “Ꮂ!” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎫᏍᏓ ᏛᎮ ᎠᎮ ᎤᎵᏍᏆᎵᏟᏗᏛᎮ ᎤᏯᎵᎦ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᎪᎯᏴᏥᏗᎤᏅᎪᏨ ᎡᏚᏥ ᎢᎾ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏓᏝᎢᏍᏛᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏒᎾᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏧᏪᏙᎸ ᏧᏒᏟᏢ ᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎢᎦ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᎾ ᏧᏄᏬ ᏥᏫᏙᎦᏁᏍᎬ ᏃᎴ ᏨᎦᎷᎬ ᏓᏁᎸ ᏧᏒᎯᎲ
segments.translation: Then, my late dad was somewhere in Arkansas. He was helping clean up those chicken houses. We went and got him, and coming back, it started raining a whole lot. There was an old building, that Robert’s Funeral Home. We stopped there. Us kids stayed in the car while the adults went inside. When we got home, the sky had all cleared up. Myself, my late dad, and my uncle George were sitting on the porch. Where my dad was sitting and I was sitting it was like this [gesture?], below us. After a while, they were talking about something when a ball of fire about this [gestures] big came around the house and went in. “Huh,” said my dad. “She came back for something she left,” he said. In a little while, it came out. My uncle, the late, used to stay there. I don’t know, for about a week he stayed at our house. When it became daytime, he would go get his clothes and then come back to our house and spend the night.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He was scared that it might bother him?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᎮᎾ ᎠᏥᎩᎳ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎦ
segments.translation: Yeah, she was a mean booger, that old woman.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Who moved into her house when she passed?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: That Lynn lives there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Wasn’t it Ice first?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏧᎩ ᎮᏃ ᏥᎬᏁᎸ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏣᏥᏁᎸ Ꮓ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏃᏭᏃ ᏧᎩ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ Ꮓ Lynn ᏣᏥᏁᎸ
segments.translation: Tsu-ki lived there. It was given to him when she passed on. Then, when Tsu-ki passed on, it was given to Lynn.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏏᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏁᎵ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎾ ᏂᎯ ᏗᏣᏁᎵᏛ?
segments.translation: He still lives there? How about your old house?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᎠᏪᏣ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎦᏁᎳ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏥᏁᎸ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏛᏃ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᎩᏰᏟᏓᏁᎮᏃ “ᏱᏓᏤᏡᏅ ᎤᎾᏭᏅ ᏄᏛᏁᏍᏗ” ᎠᏪᎵᎲ
segments.translation: My daughter lives there. I gave her that house. It just does nothing for me now. “It would be better. She would be close by,” I thought.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It would be lonely, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Lonely.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᎯᏐᏕ ᏞᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ, ᏖᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ Bob Pettit ᏥᏔᎦ ᏕᏥᏯᎧᏁᎸ “Ꭵ ᎠᏂᏨᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏍᏗᎾᏝᎢ ᏥᏈᏯ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏱᏕᏣᏚᎵᏍ?” – “ᎥᎥ ᏕᎭᏘᏃᏢᎢ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ Boy ᎤᏲᏛ ᎠᏩᏓᏅᏛᏛ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏝ ᎠᏪᏙᎳ ᏢᏅ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏱᏄᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Yeah, lonely. And I didn’t want that. A while back, I gave chickens to Bob Pettit, roosters. “We have too many roosters,” I told him. “Would you want them?” I asked. “Yes, bring them on down,” he said. Boy, I had a bad feeling around that place. I went, and it was not the same as it was.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s what will happen to you, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᎯᏐᏗᏭ ᏅᏁᎲᏂ ᏛᎮ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᎬᏴᎵ ᏛᎮ ᏭᏟ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᏣᎾᏂᎩᏃ ᎤᏲᏟᏭ ᎨᎰ ᏢᎮᏂ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᏢᎮᏂ ᏴᏩ ᏱᏚᎾᏓᎨᏳ ᎠᎾᎵᏒᏢᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ. ᏢᏅ ᏯᏁᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᏢᏅ ᏱᏗᏫᏛᎯᏅ ᎯᏲᎱᏒ ᏢᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏓᎨᏗ ᏰᎯ ᎲᏍᎫ ᎩᎶ ᎰᏩ ᏱᏙᎬᏓᏛᏂᎸᎩᏭ ᏍᎫ ᏳᎾᏓᎪ ᎯᎤᏭᏅ ᏱᎾᏛᎦ ᎾᎾᏓᏙᏢᎬᏂ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ Ꮓ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᏩᏛᏃ ᎤᏁᎸᎩᏭ ᏩᏂᎶᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᏁᎵ ᎢᎨᎵᏍᎪᏭ
segments.translation: Lonely place now that the old people don’t live there. Mostly when they pass on, it’s sad because nowadays, people have no love for each other. They fight over everything. They don’t realize you’re not going to take it with you when you die. There’s no love existing - no one will accept who you are when they see you. They would do this [gestures], as if they didn’t know you. Nowadays, I don’t even say anything, and they just go on. “Guess that’s what they think,” I just think.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Wonder how come it’s like that?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏗᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏢᏅ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏳᏰᏟᏗ ᏲᏨᏓ ᏃᎴ ᏱᏓᏤᏟ ᏲᏰᎸ ᏂᎦᏗᏅ ᏌᏭᏭ ᏏᏓᏁᎸᏭᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏙᏓᎦᏕᎴᏅᏂ ᏂᎦᏓᏅ ᏗᎦᏓᎪᎲ ᏥᏕᎦᏍᏗᎬ ᏃᎴ ᏕᎩᏴᏡᏛ ᏃᎴ ᏕᎦᏣᎦᏃᏗᏍᏛ
segments.translation: I don’t know, there’s no use acting like you’re better than others. We’re all just one, like family. We’ve all of us seen each other when we were kids with snotty noses. [laughter] Messy hair all the time.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Or a dirty face. [laughter]

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: You really were.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏮᎩᏃᎲᎵ, ᏙᏅ ᎤᏍᏗᏅ ᏚᎾᏙᎡ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ ᏣᎳᎩ Ꮕ ᎬᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏣᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᎠᏩᏅᏖ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏎ ᎬᏯᏛᏗ
segments.translation: I got told on. [more laughter] What were your parents’ names in English and in Cherokee? I know, but I have to ask.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: George Glass, Mary Killer ᎢᎾ ᏭᏕ ᎠᎬᏱ Ꮎ Mose Killer ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎤᏠᎩ ᎨᎮ
segments.translation: George Glass. Mary Killer – [was her] last name, at first. That Mose Killer, she was his aunt.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎥᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ Ꮎ ᎬᏗ Ꮩ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ?
segments.translation: Yeah, and names in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᏓᏌᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᎨᎰᎩ
segments.translation: U-da-sa-d(a) late, and my mom’s Ke-ho-g(i).

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎨᎰᎩ ᏙᏳᏛ ᎤᎾᏓᏅᏘ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎩᎸᏩᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎣᎨᏓᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ
segments.translation: They were really nice. We really liked going there.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏧᏂᏝᎾᎣ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎲᎾᏍᎫ ᎭᏢᏛ ᏗᎦᎶᏍᎪ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏰᎳ ᏃᏭᏥᎦ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏯᏩᏓᏅᏖᏟ ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ orange ᎾᏅ apples ᏒᎦᏔ ᏥᏚᏂᏩᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎩᎶᏅ ᏳᏪᏙᎳ ᏥᏓᏅᏓᏁᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ. “ᏣᏅᏗᏍ ᏙᎬᏲᎬᏛᏒ?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᏞᏍᏕ ᎥᎸᎯᏳ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎣᎩᏂᎬᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎡᎵᏌ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎬᏛᎯᏍᏛᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎡᏥ ᎡᏙᏗᏅ ᎠᎬᏯ ᏚᏂᏲᎱᏎ ᎾᎮᏅ ᏦᏍᏛᏓᎸ ᎦᎵᏉᎦ ᏳᏕ-- ᎠᏯᏛ ᎦᎵᏉᎦ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ. ᎤᏥ ᎤᏙᏓ ᏅᏁᎲᎾ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏁ. ᎾᏅᏅ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ ᎤᏍᏗᏭᏅ ᎨᎮ
segments.translation: They would have food on the table all the time. We never would think, “Where is the money coming from?” Nowadays, when I think about it, at Christmas time they would buy oranges and apples. If someone came by, they would give them to them. And, my late mom told me one time, “Do you know, as we grew up, we were never in need of anything. My late grandma raised us up,” she said. “My mom and dad passed on first, my sister was seven--no, I was seven years old.” She told me her mom and dad passed away, and her sister was little, then.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏅᎾ ᏏᏉᏲ ᏂᎨᎬᏛᏁ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎤᎵᏌ ᎤᏙᏗᏅ ᎢᎾ ᏚᎾᏛᎯᏍᏛᏁ “ᏍᎩᏅ ᏏᏉᏲ ᏬᎩᏴᏝ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏂᎦᏓ ᎥᎩᎦᎵᏎᎸ ᎠᎩᏍᏗᎬ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎲᎴᏅ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏫᎾᏮᎨᏫᏌ” ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᏙᎩᎸᏂᎲ ᎮᏂ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏲᎩᏬᏂᏌ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮲ ᎢᎾᏴᏃ ᎤᏂᎷᏨ ᎡᎵᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏙᎦᏘᎾᏫᏛᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎩᎵ ᏅᎮ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏚᏅᏁᎸ ᎪᏪᎳ Ꮓ ᎣᎦᏂᎩᏒ ᏂᎦᏓ” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: They were all sent to Sequoyah, but the little ones, her grandma and grandpa raised them up. “We all went into Sequoyah, all of my hair was cut off,” she said. “I almost forgot I was Cherokee,” she said. “They whipped us if we spoke Cherokee,” she said. “But sometime later, they came, my late grandma, and took us home. Had just got done with paperwork, and then we went home, all of us,” she said.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎡᎵᏌ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸ “ᎠᏮᏎ ᏥᏯᎥ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎩᎶᏪ ᏧᎷᏨ ᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏌᏭᏭ Ꮕ ᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᎦᏁᎴ--ᎠᏂᏁᎴ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ “ᏍᎩᏅ ᏙᏱ ᏭᎦᏔ ᏴᏫ Ꮎ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᎦᏙᎨ” ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᎡᎵᏭᏍ ᏱᎦᏍᏕᎳ ᎡᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏗᎬᎦᏎᎯᏌ ᏗᏤᏅᎲ” ᎠᎪᎮᎴᏅ ᎤᎵᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ “Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗᏅ ᎮᎵᏍᎨᎢ?” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ Ꮕ ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᎠᎦᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎦ Ꮫ ᎤᏄᎸᎲᏍᎦ ᎠᏓᏘᏅᏍᎬ” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ Ꮕ ᎤᎵᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᏅ “ᎰᏩᏭ” ᎤᏛᏁᏅᎾ ᎡᏥ ᎤᎵᏌ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏭᏅᎪᏥᏭ Ꮲ ᏳᎾᏖ ᎤᎾ ᏭᎶᏒ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏂᎦ ᎸᏢ ᎠᏍᏓᎬᎸ Ꮎ “ᎭᏫᎾ ᎣᏍᏗᏯᎡ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗᏅ ᎠᏝᎾᎡ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᏛᎨᎲ ᎠᏝᏂ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏱᏣᏲᏏ ᎭᎵᏍᏛᏡᎦ ᏙᏴᏣᏛᏅᏍᏛᏂ ᎩᎵᎾ ᏱᏍᎩᏍᏕᎸᎰᎩ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎲᎵᏍᏕᎸᎲᏭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏂᎬᎮᏂ ᏒᎩ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ ᏳᏍᏗᏭᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏢᎾᎡ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏍᎩᏃ ᏛᎩᏯᏅᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏭᏴᏞ ᏫᏚᏍᏕᎸᎮ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏕᎲᏍᎬ. “ᏍᎩᏃ ᎣᎩᏍᏆᏓ ᎣᎩᏍᏉᏙᏂ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏂᎬᎩᏪᎮᎸ “ᎮᎲᎢ ᏂᎯ ᏑᏓᏁᎸ ᎢᏤᎲ Ꮲ ᎭᎸᎯᏳ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎢᏥᏂᎬᎦ ᏱᎨᎮᏍᏗ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎢᏥᏙᎯ ᎢᏤᎮᏍᏗ” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ ᏍᎫᏭᏅ ᏂᎦ ᎠᎾᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᏩᏴᎯᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎤᏔᏂ ᎧᏁᏌ ᎧᎵ ᏗᎾᏬ ᏕᎬᎸᏛ ᏙᏥᏁᏍᎬ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏃᎦᏛᏂᏅ ᎤᎾ ᏙᏧᎶᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎩᎶ ᎴᏱ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏯᏂᏲᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎠᏎᎠᎾ ᎡᏚᏓ Ꮕ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎵᏣᏙᏂᏙᎯᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏄᏓᎴᏅ ᏏᎾ ᎨᎮ “ᏙᏗᎦᎶᏍᎨ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏙᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎠᎵᏍᎪᏅ ᎮᏂ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ ᏥᏥᏃᎮ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎨᎦᏟᎶᏍᏛᏅ ᏦᏍᏕ ᏚᎾᏄᏩ ᎤᎵᏌ Ꮕ ᏦᎨᎲ ᏫᏚᏯᏟ. ᎦᎵᏦᏕᏅ ᎤᏪᏘ ᎠᏂᏁᎵ ᎭᏢᏅ ᏱᎬᏂᎩᏒᎲᎦ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᎩᏍᎬᎾ ᎡᏚᏓ ᏗᎾᏬᏅ ᏕᎦᎸ ᎪᎵ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎾᏅᎾ ᏥᎪᏢ Ꮎ New Baptist ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᎵᏣᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᎨᎮ ᎤᎾᎾ
segments.translation: Then, one time, my mom said, “My grandma told me ‘I was all alone in the house,’ she said. ‘It felt like someone came in,’ she said.” They just lived in a one-room house, the elders. When she looked outside, a little person was standing there, she said. ‘Would you help me here? They pointed for me to come to your house,’ they told Grandma [Marlene’s mother’s grandmother]. ‘What do you think?’ she said to him. ‘My wife is having trouble having baby,’ he said to her grandma. “OK,” said my mom’s grandma. Soon as she went out, she didn’t know which way she went, just somewhere, a bluff. “We were deep down,” she said. “Food was on the table,” she said, “everything was on it.” – “If you’re hungry, sit down, we’re going to get ready. Then you can come help us,” he said. “Help yourself to anything.” Wild onion, about everything wild was on the table. “Then they called me,” she said. She went in and helped deliver the baby. “Then when we were done with it they told me, “As long as you live, your family will never be without anything,” he said. “You will live healthy,” she was told. That’s all she remembers, going in her house, she said. Then at times, a big box of clothes would come to us, she said. We didn’t know where it came from, she said. Or someone would bring food to us, but my grandpa was a preacher. “But it was different, they came from somewhere,” she said. Really, this is no lie I’m telling. In my mom’s picture, they have on really good clothes, and my grandma, the house they live in is old. Where can they get things like that? She was saying that. And he would leave, my grandpa. She said, “Clothes would still come,” she said. You know that church, there, New Baptist? He was their first preacher there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: U-da-sa-d(a)?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, Ꮎ Edward Longbird ᏧᏙᎩᏓ Ꮎ ᎡᏥ ᎤᏚᏓ ᏳᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎮᏅ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.translation: No, Edward Longbird was his name. He used to be my mom’s grandpa, and he was the first preacher there.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s good things happening to them.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩᏛᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏃᎬᏛᏅ ᏙᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎠᎾᏂᎩᏐᏂ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵᏅ ᎨᎮ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎵ ᏣᏁᎵ ᏣᏁᎵ ᏍᎪᎯ ᎠᎮ ᏳᎾᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎭ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏓᎾᏂᎩᏐᏂ ᎠᎾᏢᏅᏢ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏱᎪᎯᏗ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᎩᎶ ᎡᎰ
segments.translation: We had it really good, then. And, really, all of them are gone, the elders. All of them, I think, were around 80 years old, all of them that are gone. In that family, that’s how long one lives, they say.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᏥᏃᎮ. ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏁᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎢᎦᏗ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏱᎰ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏄᏰᏢᏛᎾ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏴᏫᏯ ᎤᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ ᏄᏛᏃ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᎢᎦᏓ ᎤᏠᏯ ᏥᎦ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏥᏕᎰᏩᏎᎪ ᎤᏂᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᎠᏁᎰᏩᏕᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎤᎾᏓᏅᏗ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ Ꭰ ᎠᏍᏃ ᏍᎩᏂ Ꭰ ᏱᏕᎯᎵᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏍᏕᎳ ᏱᏙᏛᎵᏍᏕᎳ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᏬᎯᏳ
segments.translation: Those little people you’re talking about, I’ve heard some are really afraid of something like that. For no reason, they say. That’s for the Indians - help the little people. They’re the same as us people - some are mean among them and some are good. That’s the way with the little people, but if you depend on them, they will help you. That’s what they say, and I believe that.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏍᎫ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏐ. ᎫᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏕᎭᎵᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎣᎩᏂᏃᏎᎸ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ Mama “ᎠᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᎮᏂ” ᎩᎶ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎨ “ᎠᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᎮᏅ ᎠᎩᏢᏤᎲ ᏪᏌᏅ ᏥᏈᏍᏓ ᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᎯᎾ ᏚᏂᎾᏝᎡ ᎯᎾ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ” ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎸ “ᏪᏌ” you know ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎸ “ᎫᏍᏕ ᎣᎩᏂᏂᎬᎦ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎠᎩᏢᏤᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎢᏥᏯᎷᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎣᎩᎾᎵᏍᏕᏝᏙᏗ” ᎨᎪᎮᎴ Ꮎ ᏪᏌ ᏒᎯᏰᏭᎡ ᎤᎾᏝᎣᏞ ᎠᏂ nurse. “ᎾᎡᏅ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎠᏂᏰᎮ ᏍᎫ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏱᏂᎨᏣᏛᏂᏌ ᎡᏍᏊ ᏪᏌ” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏕᏥᎾᏝ ᏪᏌ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᏅᏏᏭ ᎠᏂᎷᎪ ᏢᏅ ᎠᏯ ᎥᎸᎯᏳ ᏫᏗᏥᏴᏅᏓ ᏱᎦ. ᎤᏅᏏ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏂᎷᎦ ᎤᏬᏟᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏰᎸᏐ Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎵ Ꮒ ᏯᏗ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ Ᏺ ᏢᏲ ᏙᎬᏩᎾᏗᏅᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏕᏥᎾᏝ ᎤᏩᏏᏭᏅ ᎤᎷᏨ Ꮎ ᎤᏂᏥ ᏚᏓᏘᏅᏅ Ꮓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏕᎦᏥᏴᏁᎸ ᏗᎦᏥᎾᎵᏛ
segments.translation: That’s the way I believe, too, you can depend on them for something. An old man told us one time, “There was an old lady,” -- this old man was telling us - “the old lady got sick on me. And this elderly woman had a lot of cats. I told my cats something. ‘We’re in need of something. The old lady got sick on me, go look for something to help us,’ I told the cats. Late that evening, the nurses came and they had food with them. Cats can do it for you, too,” he said. All the time I have cats, but they come on their own. Never have I gone and got them, they will come on their own. My husband thinks it’s funny. “Look!” he’d say, but it’s good that they won’t have little ones like I have. The mother came on her own, and when she had little ones, we had all of them fixed.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎨ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏁᎸ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏳᎷᏥ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᎩᏟ ᏪᏌ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎢᎨᎰ
segments.translation: That’s what I’ve heard - if it comes on its own, a dog or cat, it’s good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Does it mean something good?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, it’s for a reason.

segments.text: ᏂᎪᎯᎸ Ꮫ ᏥᎦᏘ ᏌᏭ ᎤᎷᎯᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏳᎷᏦ
segments.translation: I’m always waiting for one to show up. But it never comes.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Me too!
I go like this [gestures] all the time. “Where is it?”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏓᏁᏠᎰᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ
segments.translation: They say they feed the little people at night.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᏒ ᏱᎦ Ꮎ ᎤᏒ ᏳᎾᎵᏍᏓᏴᏂ Ꮲ ᏯᏂᏅᎬᎵᎰ
segments.translation: When they eat supper, they don’t clean the table off. They just leave food on the table.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Marlene, ᎦᎾᏫᎵ,
Marlene Glass, Dianna Guffey,
They just leave food on the table.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s why.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: (…) some [people].

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏥᏄᏍᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎫᏍᏓᏭ ᎠᎾᏬ ᎬᏗ ᏧᏩᏄᏢᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᏩᏛᏒ
segments.translation: That’s the way it was. They would cover it with just some cloth. That’s the way it was as I grew up.

segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛᎮ ᏳᏍᏓ Ꮎ ᎣᏂ ᏯᏝ ᎦᏚ ᏳᏩᎦᏞᏌᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎮᏍᏓ Ᏺ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏍᏗ ᎯᎯᏴ ᏍᏗ ᎯᎯᏴ ᎯᎯᏯᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᏱᏩᎩᏞᏌ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏄᏰᏟᏕ “Ꮩ ᏍᎩᎾ?” ᎨᎵᎲ ᏂᎦᏗᏅ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ ᎨᎲ [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ]
segments.translation: Guess that’s why. If I picked up the last of the bread from the table, my mom would say, “Don’t get all of it. Leave some on the table,” she would tell me. “How come?” I thought. I was wanting all of it. [laughs]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Because you were hungry!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I’m saying, “I’m hungry!”
“Haw! Leave it be!”

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ ᎣᎩᎾᎵ ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᏱᏩᎩᏒᏝ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᎦᏛᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏱᏄᏅᎾ ᏲᎦᎵᏍᏓᏴᏃᏂ, “ᏙᎨ ᏂᏥᏅᎦᎵᎲᏂ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “ᏍᎫᏭᏅ ᎮᏂ ᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᎩᎵ ᏌᎾᎴ” ᏍᎩᏃ ᏥᏩᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏓᏁᏠᎲ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ
segments.translation: That friend of mine, when I used to stay the night there, that’s the way it would be after we ate. “How come you don’t clean it up?” I’d say. [laughter] “It’s going to be that way until the morning.” That’s when I realized they were feeding the little people.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎩᎶ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎬᎩᎾᏝᎥ brick layer ᏥᎨᏒ Ꭵ ᏥᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏧᎵᏌ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎨ ᎤᏃᎮᏢᏅ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎤᎾ ᏌᎷᏂᎨᏴ ᎾᎠ ᎤᏂᎳᏂᏏᏞ ᎠᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎸᏢᏴ ᏥᏭᏟᎶᎢᏕᎴ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᎨᏒ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᎠᎾᏛᎩᏍᎬ ᎤᏂᎾᏫᏍᏛ Ꮎ ᎤᎾᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏗᏝ and a ᏃᏭᏅ ᎢᎦ ᏥᏚᏂᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎨᎮ and a ᏃᎴ ᎩᎶ ᏍᎢ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏣᏥᏃᏎᎸ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏱᏣᎯᏯᏍᏛᏂ ᎡᏝᏪ ᏱᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓ ᏙᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎸ ᏙᏭ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏛᏅᏍᎬ yeah
segments.translation: One time, I worked for some whites. I was a brick-layer. One was talking about his grandparents. They moved close to Sallisaw, and later on, they kept hearing talking and cutting up coming from the kitchen. Then it really scared them, and they were white. Then they told another white person. “If you leave out something to eat, it will get quiet,” [they were told]. And that’s what they did, and after that, it got quiet.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ. ᎭᎸᎯᏳ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏯᏂᎶᎯᏍᏓ ᎠᎬᏯ ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏓ ᏯᎾᏓᏮᏛᎯᏓ ᏯᏅᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏧᏂᏲᎱᏒ ᏱᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎨᏨᏂ ᏗᏝ ᏃᎴᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᏛᏛᎦᏂ Ꭰ ᏯᏕᎳᎰᎯ ᏍᎫ ᏴᏓᎭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏗᏖᎵᏙ ᏱᎦ ᏱᏚᏂᏃᏟᏍᏓ Ꮓ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏛᎪᏗ ᎨᎰ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏥᏍᏆ ᏱᎦ Ꮎ ᏥᎦᎵᎵ ᏱᏂᎦᏪ ᏃᏭᎮᏃ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏪᏙᎵᏠ Ꮓ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏃᏭᏅᏃ ᏅᏱ ᏱᏗᏧᏖᏏ
segments.translation: Sometimes, they say, at times, they might stop by, the ones that left before us. They’d come and see us, they used to say. Ones that have died and kin to you. Or when you’re going to hear about something, you’ll know by that, like rattling the dishes, that you’re going to hear something [news], they would say. And, like a bird, that chickadee, if it hollers, that’s when someone is coming. That’s when you start picking up rocks. [laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Then nobody will come over!

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎮᏅ ᏥᎾᏂᏪᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏥᎦᎵᎵ ᎩᎶ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏪᏙᎵᏠ ᏣᏩᏛᎯᏙ ᏯᎾᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: That’s what they used to say. “If a chickadee is hollering, someone is coming to visit you,” they would say.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎨ ᏥᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᏣᏛᏓᏍᏓ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᏣᏃᎯᏌ ᏄᏓᎴᏒ
segments.translation: That’s what my dad used to talk about. “Listen good to something and it will tell you all things.”

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, all things.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏳᏍᏗ ᏭᎨᎲ, ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᏥᏍᏆ Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏚᎾᏙᎥ ᏂᎪᎸ Ꮫ ᏯᏁᏡᎲᎦ ᎠᏮᎨᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏚᎾᏙᎥ
segments.translation: All things. Also, those little birds - I don’t know what they’re named, - all the time they will holler, I forgot what they’re called.
E-li-ta-mi – Wren, right?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: That’s it, I think.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: E-li-ta-m(i) – Wren.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏯᏁᏡᏂᏓᏛ ᎤᏓᏈᏍᏓᏛ ᏱᎾᏂᏩ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏳᏓᎭᏭᏛ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎨᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏦᏎᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏃᎴ ᎩᎶ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᏦᏎᏓ ᏱᏓᎧᏃᎮᏢᏂ ᏃᎮᏃ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏂᎬᏩ. ᏳᏓᎭᎮᏂ “Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᏃᏎᎠ ᏥᏍᏆ?!” ᏱᏫᎦᏥᏲᏌ ᎮᏂ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᏛᎪᏗ ᎨᎰ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᏦᏎᏓ ᏱᏮᎭᏛᎦᎦ
segments.translation: They will come hollering, their holler is really irritating, but sometimes they’re telling you something. Even if it’s bothersome, or someone might tell you something bothersome, that’s when it will holler. Sometimes, “What are you telling me, bird?!” I’d say to them. Too, you will hear something bothering, you could hear.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎾᏛᏲ ᏓᏁᎸ Ᏺ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏩᎱ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏂᎬᏪ
segments.translation: At my house, a screech owl is hollering all the time.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏣᏅᏗᏍᏅ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᏥᏓᏂᎪᏩᏗᏍᎬ ᎤᎾᏍᏛᎶᎬ ᏗᏝ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏗᏝ ᏙᎨ ᏴᏓ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ Bigfoot ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎪ
segments.translation: Do you know that thing they’d see in the mountains, in the woods, how would you say in Cherokee, Bigfoot?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Oh, those big feet.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏧᎳᏍᏕᏂ, ᎴᏱᎦ. ᎾᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏅ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᏚᏠᏯᏍᏕ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.translation: Or “Di-s-du-le-n(a)” [laughter] I believe on that the little people include that.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Me too, I’ve heard that.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᎠᏬᎯᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᏠᏯᏍᏓ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ... ᎩᎶᏩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏯᎵᏛᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩᏴ ᏭᎵᏍᏓ ᎡᏆ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᏯᎵᏛᏗ
segments.translation: I believe it includes the little people. It will disappear real quick. That big something just disappears.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮲ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ like ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏪᎵᏌ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮎ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏦᏍᏗᏁᎸ. ᏍᎫ ᎾᏥᎦᏅᎾ ᏦᏍᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏝ ᏧᎶᏎ ᎤᏗᎵᎬ ᏗᏝ. ᎠᎹᏱ Ꮎ ᎡᎦ ᎡᎵᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏴᏖᎾ ᎤᎾ ᏧᏪᏴ “ᎫᏍᏕ ᏅᏯ ᎤᏔᎾ ᏛᏳᏗᏅᎲ ᎾᏅ ᎦᎢᏒ ᎤᎾ ᏚᏥᏢ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎮᏍᏕ ᏱᎦᎵᏍᎪᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏅᎯᏒ Ꭱ ᏗᎦᏗᏢᏍᏗ ᏦᏍᏕ ᏱᎩᏓ ᏅᏯ ᏙᏗᏳᏕᎬ” ᏣᏬᏎᎲ
segments.translation: I never thought about it, but near our first home, that road we were talking about, he [my husband] had come from that direction. On the west side, a creek is running. It’s pretty wide, that creek. “Something threw a big rock, and it landed where I was walking,” he said. “I’m not lying. I ran all the way here. It was throwing good-sized rocks,” he told me.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Ꮎ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ Ꮎ ᏥᎦᏅᏂ Ꮎ Starkiller ᏥᎦᏅᏂ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ “ᎩᎶ ᎤᏍᏗ pickup ᎤᎾᏦᏕ ᎾᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏯ “ᎬᏕᎳᎣᏍᎬᏅ ᎡᎳᏗᏅ ᏂᏙᎩᏅᏅ ᎡᎦᎮᏂ ᎤᏁᎩᏟᏓ ᎤᏒᏥᏢ” ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᏒᏃᏱ Ꮎ ᎨᎲ ᏢᏅ ᏯᏩᎾᏘ ᏄᏰᏟᏛ ᎤᎾ ᏥᏃᎦᏕᏲᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᎫᏍᏕ ᎣᎩᎾᏣᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᎣᎾᏗᏝ ᎣᎩᎾᏦᏛ” ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᏙᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎦᎨᏓ ᎨᎮ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏎᎾ ᎤᎾ ᎩᎳᏫᏴ ᎤᎵᏛᏗᏅᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏍᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏅ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏴᏫ. ᎠᏩᎾᏘᏅ ᎬᏩᎾᎵᏣᎪᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᎨᎲ. ᎾᎡᏲ ᎣᎩᎾᏁᎳᏛ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏘ
segments.translation: Then, one time, on Starkiller Road, they were saying that some people were in a small pickup. One woman said, “I could tell, we had the windows down. And there was a real bad smell that came,” she said. “It was midnight. I don’t know why we went around that way,” she said. [laughter] “Something got in the back of our ride, and it was real heavy, too,” she said. “But, quickly, it jumped out,” she said. That’s all I’ve heard them talking about it, and I know that they wouldn’t lie. But I don’t know about the one I was married to.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He might be lying!

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: He might be lying to me!
That’s how your husband was.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎠᏎᎾ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏂᎬᏪᏍᎬᎢ “ᏧᏔᏂ ᏅᏱ ᏥᏙᏗᏳᏕᎬ ᎣᏍᏓᏅ ᏍᏓᏯ ᏤᏕᎦᏥᎯᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: But that’s what he was saying, “Big rocks it was throwing, good and hard they would land,” he said.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᎫ Levi ᎡᏙᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎡᏙᏙ, ᎯᏲᎵᎦ Ꮫ Levi? I guess ᏩᏓᏟᏎ ᎤᎾ Star killer road ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏮᏣᏁᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: Also, Levi was at my dad’s sometimes. You know Levi, don’t you?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: I guess ᏩᏗᏟᏎ ᎤᎾ Starkiller road ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏮᏣᏁᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: He was driving on Star killer. “Something got in with me,” he said.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏭ ᏛᎮ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏄᏂᏪᏎ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎤᏝᏛᏗᏅᎮ ᏣᎾᏗᎲ ᎮᏂ. ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎮ
segments.translation: Might be that, too, that’s what they said. But then it jumped out, they said. That’s where it was.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: “ᏙᏍᏓᏗᏟᏒᏭ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏥᏍᎦᏱᎲᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎯᎤᏭ ᎾᏮᏛᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᎨᏭᏃ ᏫᏓᎦᎴᏫᏍᏔᏂ ᎭᏠᏒᏭ! ᏥᏲᎮᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᏩᏮᎴᏫᏍᏛᏅ Ꮓ ᏣᏗᎲ ‘ᎭᏠ ᏃᏩᏥᎦ!’ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏙᏅ ᎤᏠᏎᏛᎮ Ꮓ ᏢᏃ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᏩᏕᎳᎰᏎ ᏣᏗᎲ. “ᎤᎾ ᏛᎮ ᎡᏙᏙ ᏘᏯᏘᎾᏫᏛᎲ” ᏥᏥᏲᏎᎲ
segments.translation: “We just kept going,” he said. “And I was scared. I was like this [gestures]. ‘I’m going to stop,’ I told it. ‘Just get out!’ I told it,” he said. “I stopped ‘Get out, now!’ I told it,” [he said]. “I guess it got out, because I never noticed anything then,” he said. “I guess you brought it to my dad’s house,” I told him.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏛᎮ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏚᎵᏍᎨ ᎤᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: And that’s where he was wanting to go, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: “That’s where I took him,” he said.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Or, “I brought him back to you,” he said.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏛᏲ ᎦᏂᏰᎩ ᏙᎭ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎫᏓᎠ. ᏙᏍᎩᏂ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ Bigfoot ᏣᏗ ᏢᏅ ᎰᏩ ᏴᏫ ᎤᏂᎪᎲ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏢᎦ ᎨᎦᏑᏰᏍᏙ Ꭸ?
segments.translation: Really is dangerous isn’t it, something like that? “Why?” I think about that Bigfoot, you’re saying. Not many people have seen it, or are they just picked out?

segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏗᏩᏁᎶᏅ ᏣᎩᏍᏗᎬ ᏍᎫ ᎩᎵᏅ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏥᏥᏴᎯᎲ ᏢᏅ ᎸᎯᏳ
segments.translation: All the time, I have played in woods when I was little, and sometimes I’d come in at night, but never had…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Me too, nothing ever…
…something like that take me.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Also, maybe…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: But I was scared, too, back then.
I went in the woods.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏫ ᏍᎫ Ꮎ like ᎩᏟ ᏱᎦ Ꮎ ᏣᎾᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᏂᎯ ᎯᏴᏫ ᎡᎵᏫ ᎮᏂᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏓ ᏯᏁᏕᎳᎰᏍᎦ
segments.translation: Maybe, like dogs can tell if you’re a good person, maybe they’re like that, they can tell.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: They can tell.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎠᎾᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᎯᏴᏩ ᏃᎴ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᏱᎦ ᏃᎴ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎡᏍᎦ ᏱᏣᏰᎳ ᏥᏂᏣᏛᎾᏕᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏄᏰᏟᏛᎾ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Ꮎ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᏣᏂᏴᎯᎰ ᏴᏫ. ᎠᎾᏕᎳ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎰ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎠᎾᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᎠᎮ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏥᏣ ᎩᎶ ᎠᏎ ᏓᎾᏟᎶᏍᏛᏅᎲᏍᎨ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎾᎠ ᏥᏥᏁᎵ ᎫᏍᏕ ᏧᏂᎨᎯᏙᎴ ᏍᎫᎮᏂ ᎨᎵ ᏄᏍᏙ ᎠᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ. ᎠᎾᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᎩᎶ Ꮩ ᏳᏰᎸ ᏳᏁᎫᏥᏭ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏄᏰᏟᏛᏂ ᏧᏂᏲᎰ ᎠᎾᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᎠᎮ ᎨᎵᎰ ᏂᎪᎸᏅ ᏓᎾᏗᏴᏛᏍᎪ ᏓᏂᏲᎲ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: They can tell if you’re a good person or if you’re mean, or if you got bad intentions for being here, for no reason. And, when people go into a cemetery, something is there and it can tell. Maybe. One time, the boys, I guess someone was taking pictures in the cemetery by my house. Something ran them off. That’s the way it is, I guess. It can tell if someone has bad intentions, or they’re looking for nothing good. They can tell, maybe. I think, all the time, it’s showing where they’re looking for them, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: They can’t see it. It hides somewhere, maybe.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: If they want you to see them, you’re going to see them.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah.
I don’t want to.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏘ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏯ
segments.translation: No, I don’t know if I want to, either.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓ ᏛᏲ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎥᏍᎦᏱᎯ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ “ᏙᎨ ᏱᎾᏛᎦ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏱᏣᎪᎯ?” ᏥᏯᏛᏛᏁᎸ “Ꮧ ᎫᏍᏓ. Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏳᏰᏟᏗ ᏲᏍᎦᎯ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᎯᎵᏃᎮᏛᏂ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏂᏣᏛᎾᏕᎬ ᏃᎴ ᏕᎱᎪᏗᏍᎬ and a ᎤᏁᎳᎩᏭ ᏱᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᎣᏏᏭ”
segments.translation: Really, my dad said it’s nothing to be afraid of. “What would you do if you seen something like that?” I asked him. “Nothing. No reason to be afraid of something like that, just talk to them. Tell them what you are doing there and what your intentions are. Then it will be OK.”

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱᏭ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᏥᎦᏗ Ꮎ ᎩᏟ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏂᎶᏍᎪ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏪᏅᎲ ᎾᎠ ᏴᏫ ᎾᏅ ᎾᎥ ᏱᏦᎦᏓᎵ ᎩᏝ ᎤᏂᎾᏝᎢ ᏍᎫ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᏦᎩᏁᏅᏒ ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᎤᏰᎸᏐ. ᏣᏅᏘᏍ ᎩᎶ Ꭱ ᏂᏚᎸᏉᏛᏂ ᏱᎦ ᏱᎦᎷᎦ. ᏃᏭᏅ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏴᏫ ᎠᏂᎷᎪ Ꮂ ᎫᏍᎠ ᏳᏪᎵᏐ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎵ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.translation: Same as what I was saying, like a dog they go by my house, people do. Our neighbor has a dog, and my house is like their house, you know? If he don’t like someone, he’ll come over. Some people come, he don’t think nothing of it. That’s how that thing is, I think.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: It knows real quick.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏲᏓᏂᎵ ᏛᏍᎫ ᏯᎾᏕᎳᎰᎯ ᎠᎭ ᎩᏟ? ᎪᏛᎮ ᎤᏒ ᎦᏚ ᏓᏥᏝᏂ [ᎤᏂᏰᏣ,ᏍᎬ] ᎤᎾᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ
segments.translation: Even when you’re sick, the dogs will know. Tonight, I’m going to put bread out. [laughter] For them to eat.
I’m going to lay bologna out for them.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Hard bread [Toast].

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏥᏃᏎ ᏗᎰᏂ, ᎦᎪᏛ ᏥᏥᏃᏎᎲ? ᎲᏍᎫ ᏲᎦᏅᏖᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ pizza ᎨᎲ ᏥᎦᏛᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏥᏓᏩᏓᏘᏅᏅ Ꮓ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏯᏂᏔᏲᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎾᏅ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎤᏫ..Ꭽ.. ᎤᏁᎩᏟᏗᏭ ᎠᏒᎦ Ꮎ ᏫᏌ” ᏯᏗ ᎮᏂ
segments.translation: I was telling someone. Who was I telling? “We didn’t know what pizza was as we were growing up.” After I had kids, then they would ask for it. Then, my late dad, “Ooh-wee! Smells bad that ‘wizza’ [pizza],” he would say.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: “Wizza!” [laughing]

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: “ᎤᏁᎩᏟᏗ ᏛᏲ ᎠᏒᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏫᏌ” ᏯᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮲ ᏳᎸᏉᏕ
segments.translation: “Really smells bad, that wizza (pizza)!” he’d say. He didn’t like it.
[more laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᎧᏲ, ᎭᎳᎩ ᏳᎾᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏣᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᏕᏣᏓᏘᎾᎥ?
segments.translation: Well! … How old did you say your kids were?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏅᎩᏍᎪᎯ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏅᎩᏍᎪᎯ ᏔᎵ
segments.translation: The girl, she will be 41 years old, and the boy is 42.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What do they do for work?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ Baldor ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᎾᏅ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎸᏢ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ Cherokee Nation
segments.translation: The boy, he works at Baldor. And the girl, she works around here somewhere; Cherokee Nation.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Do they have kids? Or…?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᏢᏲ ᏨᎩᎵᏌ ᏯᏁᎭ. ᏍᎫᏅ Florene Ꮎ ᏧᎵᏌ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ “ᎾᏂ” ᎬᏬᏎᎰ. ᎤᏂᏥ ᎮᏂ, ᏦᎢ ᎮᏂ ᎾᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᎤᏂᏥ ᎮᏂ ᏧᏂᎩᏒ ᏦᎤᏭ ᏳᏗᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ eighteen Ꮓ ᎨᎵ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ. ᎤᏂᏥ ᏧᏂᎩᏒ ᏍᎩᏅ ᎦᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲᏭ ᏗᏔᎯᏍᏛᏅ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏳᎾᏚᎵ
segments.translation: No, they don’t, I don’t have grandkids. That Florene? Her grandkids call me “Nani.” Their mom--there are three of them girls. Their mother left when the three year-old was little, she’s 18 now, I think. Their mom left them, so I was just helping to raise them up. If they need something.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s good. … Tell us about you going to school.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏏᏉᏲ ᏥᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆᎥ Ꮓ ᏣᏁᎵᏁ ᏥᏓᎩᏍᏆᏛ ᎪᎢ ᎾᎮᏂ ᏥᎩᎾᏕᎳᏆᎥᎢ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ Mitch ᎠᏫ ᏏᏉᏲ
segments.translation: I went to school at Sequoyah. After I got done with eighth grade at Greasy, I went to school with Mitch at Sequoyah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Poor you. Not really, I’m just kidding.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: “ᏝᏍ ᏱᏍᏉᏟᎩ?” ᏣᏬᏎᎲ, ᏥᏆᏁᎶᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎠᏮᎨᏫᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏚᏙᎥ
segments.translation: “Don’t you recognize me?” he said to me. I didn’t recognize him and forgot what his name was.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: She said, “Hello, Bill!”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: “ᏍᎩᏍ ᏂᎯ?” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ... ᏍᎩᏅ ᏐᎢᎾ ᏃᎴᏛ ᎠᏫ ᏥᏓᎩᏍᏆᏛ Okmulgee tech ᏥᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆᎥ ᏥᏓᎩᏍᏆᏛ ᏃᎴ Stillwell ᏥᏮᎩᎶᏒ
segments.translation: “Isn’t that you?” I said. When I got done over here [Sequoyah HS], I went to school at Okmulgee Tech. After I got done there, I went to Stilwell.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did you play ball here?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᎾᎡ ᏏᏉᏲ Ꭱ Ꮎ basketball ᏃᎴ Ꮎ ‘drill team’ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᏍᎫ ᎤᎾ ᏥᎨᎸ
segments.translation: Yeah, at Sequoyah, basketball, and I was in a ‘drill team’ they call it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: (???) you were throwing it.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏃ ᏕᏣᏍᏆᏗ ᎭᏢ Ꮓ ᏕᏣᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴ Ꮓ?
segments.translation: Then when you got done with that, where did you work?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: CNI ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎯᏍᎩ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏃᎴ Tyson Ꭲ ᏧᏛᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ Ꮓ Stillwell foods ten years ᏍᎪᎯ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎪᎯ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏃᏭᏃ Ꮎ ᎥᏳᎩ ᏧᎯᎶᏢ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꮩ ᏥᏂᎬᏛᏁᎸ ᏣᎩᏑᎵᎩᏨ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎮᏍᏓ ᎤᎾ ᏥᎮᏏ ᏥᏙᏣᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎵᏏ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎳ ᏙᎯᏳ ᏍᎫ Ꮲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏰᏣᎦᏎᏍᏗ ᏥᏚᏂᏲᎱᏒ ᎮᏂ ᏦᎢ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏙᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏥᏗᏂᏢᏨ ᎥᏳᎩ. ᏃᏭᏃ ᎠᏬᏢᏭ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᏚᏩ ᏛᎬᎩᏯᏅᎲ ᏱᏣᏚᎵ ᏗᏤᏅᎲᏭ ᏱᏕᏣᎸᏫᏍᏓᏏ ᎬᏬᎮᎸ ᎾᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᎾᏗᎵᏍᎬ ᎦᏥᏍᏕᏟᏗ Ꮎ ᎦᏬᏂᏓ ᏗᎪᏪᎳᏅ ᏗᎪᎵᏰᏗ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ. ᏃᏭᏃ Ꮎ Stillwell ᎣᎪᏢ ᏦᏥᏍᏕᏟᏗ ᏴᏫ Ꮎ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎪᏪᎳ ᎤᏚᏟᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏱᏄᎾᏛᏂ ᎠᎹ ᏱᎦ ᎠᎾᎦᎵᏍᎦ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎠᏈᏴᎲᎾ ᏕᎦᏥᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏗᎧᎵᏏᏌᏅ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎤᏃᎪᏗ ᎠᏁᎯ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎬᎦᏑᏰᏒ
segments.translation: I worked at Cherokee Nation Enterprises [CNI] for five years. Then I worked at Tyson. Stilwell Foods for 10 years, then CNI for 10 years. Then that virus got here, we all got laid off, but I just quit. “Don’t go back there to work,” said my husband. “They don’t watch you all very well.” Three died there where we worked, they got sick with the virus. Then I just stayed home. Then Keetoowah’s [United Keetoowah Band; UKB] called me. “If you want to, you can work from home,” they said. They wanted my help with something. They wanted things written or read in Cherokee. That’s what I started doing. Then at Stilwell, we have a place to help people, like paperwork if they’re in need to pay for things - water or electric. I help fill out paperwork there. A lot of them just speak Cherokee, that’s why they picked me.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Good, it’s good what you’re doing.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏦᎢ ᏅᎩ ᏛᎮᏃ ᎾᎠ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎰ
segments.translation: Three or four, close to four years I’ve been doing that.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Keetoowah Band?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Keetoowah Band?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, we’re Keetoowah.

segments.text: ᎤᎾ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏱᏬᏥᏙᎾ Marlene ᏗᏯᎥ Marlene
segments.translation: We stand around there all the time, where Marlene’s office is.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We’ll be standing there, too!
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Which one do you like best, what you’ve done, where you’ve worked?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎯᎢ Ꮫ ᏥᏂᎦᏛᏁ ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏙ “ᏴᏫ ᎮᏂ ᎦᏥᏯᏙᎵᎪ” ᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎵ ᎣᏍᏓᏓᏅᏖ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏗᏭᏃ ᎧᎵ Ꮓ ᏙᎯ ᏲᎩᎾᏛᏁᏗ ᏙᎩᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ “ᏙᏓᏂᎦᏴᎳᏥ ᎮᏂ ᎲᏍᎫ ᏱᎩᎾᏘᏭ ᏍᎫ ᎡᏘᏴ Ꮲ ᎠᎮ ᏍᏊ ᏗᎾᏓᏙᏟᎩ ᏱᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏕᎩᎾᏓᎧᏁᏍᏗ ᏗᎾᏓᏙᏝᎬᏄᏭ Ꮓ” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “ᏱᏓᏤᏟᏅᎲᏭ ᏙᎢ ᏱᏂᎩᎾᏛᏁᎳ ᏕᎩᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ Ꮟ ᎣᏍᏓᏭ ᏥᎦ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏱᏥᏍᏕᎵᎰ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏩᏕᏔᏁᎰ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎮᏂ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ, – “Mom, ᎬᎵᎡᎵᏤᎡ ᏥᏍᎩᏍᏕᎵ” ᎠᏬᎮᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ, well ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎯᎢ ᏖᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᎫᏔ ᎾᎮᎾ ᎠᎹᏟᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᏨᏱᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᏳᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏫᏥᎩᎡᎳ. “ᏩᏙ Mom ᎢᎦ ᎬᎵᎡᎴᏤᎰ ᏥᏍᎩᏍᏕᎵ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “Ꮧ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᎨᎵ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏢᎮᏂᏴ ᏓᎫᏔᏂ ᏃᏭᏃ ᏥᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᎫᏅ ᏗᏩᏠᏍᏗ ᏱᏓᏩᏚᎵ ᏦᎩᎾᏠᏍᏗ ᏱᏙᎩᏂᎷᎶᏤ ᏱᏙᏛᎯᏅᏍᏗ ᎸᏢ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ, “Ꭽ! Mom!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ
segments.translation: This, what I’m doing now, I really like it. “I feel sorry for people,” I was telling my husband. We’re thinking about just completely laying off from work. “We’re going to get old. We don’t even know, a year from now we may not know each other. Looking at one another, not knowing each other,” I tell him. “Better we lay off working while it’s still good,” I told him. And I help the boy. I get worried cause he’s working by himself. “Mom, I’m thankful to you for helping me,” he says at times. Well, a while back when it snowed, he didn’t have a light, so I went and got it for him. “Thank you, Mom. I really appreciate you helping me out,” he said. “I don’t mind,” I told him. “Someday it’s going to snow, and then I’m going to be old. I might want “Di-wa-tlo-s-da-wu” – [Diapers for me] or we’ll both need them, and you can pick them up,” I told him. [laughter] “Haw! Mom!” he said.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They don’t speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏣᏅᏘᏍ ᎾᎡ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏃᏭᏅ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᏓᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᏃᏢ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᏍᎨ. ᎢᎦ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎦᏬᏂ ᎾᏅ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏍᏆᏟᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ ᏱᎦ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏰᎵᏍᎨ ᏣᏓᏟᏙᎲ ᏂᎬ ᎠᏁᏦᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎾᎮᏂ ᎪᎢ ᏥᏓᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ football ᎮᏂ ᏣᏁᏦᏍᎬ quarter back ᎢᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: You know, the boy, he used to speak. Then he started going to school, then he wasn’t speaking it. He spoke really good. And the girl, if it wasn’t ball, she didn’t care. She ran around playing ball. She was going to school there at Greasy. She played football there, she was the quarterback.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Really? [laughs]

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᏂᎬ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏁᏦᏂᏙᎲ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᎦᏎᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏧᏣ Ᏺ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᏒᏃ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᏓᏕᎳᏆᎲ ᏭᏩᎨᏫᏐᏁ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏱᏥᏍᏆᏂᎪᏍᎪ ᏱᏛᎧᏁᎦ. ᏣᏅᏘᏍ Ꮎ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏙᎵᎦ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ Ꮟ ᎪᎵᎪ ᎰᎵᎩᏍ ᏥᏂᏥᏪ?
segments.translation: Yeah, she played all around. She didn’t pay attention to anything. The boy, he was good, but then when he started school, he forgot all of it [Cherokee]. But sometimes it amazes me. He’ll speak, you know, like how we [all] understand it? That’s how he understands. Do you understand what I’m saying?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏥᎪᏩᏗᎰ ᎢᎦᏓ Ꮭ ᏯᏃᏟᎪ ᏥᏙᏝᎦ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎢᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏳ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᏄᎾᎵᏑᏯᏩᏕᎬᎾ ᎨᎮᏍᏓ ᏞᏍᏕ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᏛᏃᎵᏣ ᎰᏝᎩᏍ ᏥᏂᏥᏪ?
segments.translation: Sometimes I see that. Some of them don’t understand like we understand. Some of them speak without it. If they don’t mix it in, they won’t understand, you know what I’m saying?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s true.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎪ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏯᏗ ᏍᎩᏃ ᏫᎦᏕᎳᎣᏍᎪ ᏏᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏄᏍᏙ ᎪᎵᏟᎪ ᏱᎨᎵᏍᎪ
segments.translation: That’s why I’m thankful. Sometimes he will say something, then I realize, “That’s the way he understands,” I think.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓ ᏛᏲ ᏥᎦᏃᎮᏍᎪ ᎬᎩᏬᎾᏗ ᎴᏱᎦ ... ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏳᎾᏓᏟᏏᏌᏂ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏚᎵᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎡᏈ ᏥᎦ ᏦᏣᎵᏍᎩᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ and ᏃᏩ ᏍᎫ ᏥᎦ ᏙᏓᏩᏍᎬ ᏯᎾᎴᎾ ᏓᏂᏬᎾᏗᏍᎬ ᏴᏫ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᏄᏓᎴᏒ ᏗᎪᏏᏌᏅ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎾᏍᎩᏂ “ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᏔᏛᏓᏍᏛᏂ” and ᎢᎦᏓ Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎮ ᎠᏩᏁᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏣᏩᏚᎵᏍᎬ ᎢᎦ ᏥᏓᎾᎵᏟᏙᎲ ᎣᎩᎾᎵ Ꮎ ᎠᏮᏌ ᏣᏬᏢ. ᎬᎩᏐᎮᎲ Ꭾ “ᎤᎾᏛ ᏔᎵᏍᏛᏡᏂ ᎲᏛᏓᏍᏓ!” – “ᎲᏅ” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ “Ꮂ ᏍᎫ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᏤ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ” ... “ᎠᏎ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏛᎪᏙᏗ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏱᏣᏛᎦᏂ ᎸᏢᏴ ᏫᏛᏟᎶᏟ ᎰᏝᎨᏍᏗ”
segments.translation: My dad used to tell, or preach to us. A long time ago, we gathered in September for our big dances. And on Sunday, they start preaching to people, or talking about different things. They talked about the events that happened. Then he told me, “But you’re going to listen.” I didn’t want to. I wanted to go play, running around with my friends. I was sitting there, alone. He got on to me. “Hey, you sit and listen!” – “But I don’t understand what they’re talking about,” I told him. “You have to listen. Sometime later, you will understand.”

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, yeah. ᏍᎩᏛ ᏄᏍᏗ ᏙᎭ? ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᏬᎯᏳ
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s the way it is, isn’t it? That’s what I believe.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ, ᎤᎪᏗ Ꭱ ᎠᏮᎨᏩᏏᏙᎸ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏁᎸ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᏳᏓᎵᎭ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᏄᏓᎴᏒ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏁᎵᏙᎸ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ ᎨᎰ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎬ
segments.translation: Really, that’s what happened. I forgot a lot of what I had heard, but sometimes I remember what I’ve heard. But I think it was meant to help me, what I remember.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭽ ᎯᎾᎾ ᏲᏁᎦᎭ ᏥᏂᏬᏂ ᎢᎾᏁᏝᏗᎮᏍᏗ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎢᎾᏝᏃᎮᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎩᎾᏑᏴᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ ᏙᏍᏛᏓᏙᎮᎰ ᏱᏫᏙᎩᏃᏝ ᏱᏫᏙᎩᏁᏰᏥᎩ “Ꭽ, Ꮂ, why?” ᏱᏫᏙᏍᏓᏙᎮ
segments.translation: That’s what we were talking about a while back. “Haw! This English that we’re speaking. Let’s try to speak to each other all the time, and not mix English with it. We’d be sitting there, just looking at each other and laughing. ‘Ha, huh, why?’ we’d be saying to each other.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You both speak English.
“But…, I mean…, And…” is what we’ll say.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, “why” we’d say to each other. We’d be talking in English.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏱᏃᎵᏍᏓᏏ ᎾᏕᎳᎰᏒᏂ ᏱᏮᎴᏂ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎥᎦᏬᏂᎲ
segments.translation: That’s what will happen. Without realizing it, you’d start speaking in English.

segments.text: Strikes ᎮᏂ ᏕᏥᏁᎰ. Ꭿ ᏂᏕᏥᏴᏁᎰ ᎦᏬᏂᎲ
segments.translation: I give her strikes when she speaks English, I go like ‘this’ [gestures] to her.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᎩᏛ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎠᎾᎵᏣᏙᎲᏍᎬ ᏍᎫ ᏦᎩᏅᏍᏛᏕᎲ ᏍᎫ ᏙᏯ ᏦᎦᏁᏟᏗ ᎠᏎᎮᏂ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎣᎩᏴᏟᎯᏍᏗ ᏃᎬᏁᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎫ ᏥᏃᎮ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎦᏘᏲ ᎦᏥᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎲ ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎠᏂ--ᏧᎾᏛᎯᏍᏓ “ᎮᏍᏗ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏱᏥᏒᏂᎨᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᏔᏂ ᎢᎾᏓ ᏕᏥᏯᏂ” ᏣᎾᏗᎲᎡ ᏣᏅᏘᏍ ᏙᎯᏳ Ꭱ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏃᏪ ᏥᎦ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏓᏂᏩᏘᎰᎡ ᏣᏁᏩ ᎢᎾᏓ ᏙᏗᏳᎾᏂᎩᏓ ᎸᏢ ᏫᏚᏂᏯᏅᏓ ᏓᎾᏘᏃᎯ ᎠᎹᏰᏟ
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s the way it is. And their preaching, too, they’d tell us not to play outside. They made us come inside. And what you were talking about, too. One time, at the stomp grounds, I went with them. They were talking, the elders. “Don’t you be whistling at night. You are calling big snakes,” they would say. You know, really it is that way. Nowadays, they find huge snakes that come from somewhere, or someone went somewhere and got them and brought them to America.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: It really is that way.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That’s true.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏅ ᏥᎾᏁᏪ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏅ “ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᏓᎾᏁᏍᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏗᎬᏁᎦᏍᏓ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ. ᎭᏢᏭᏍ ᏱᏂᏣᎶᏏ ᎸᏢᏛ ᏂᎬ ᏙᏛᎳ ᏧᏬᏚᏨ Ꮫ ᏙᏗᏓᏁᎵ ᏝᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏕ ᎪᎯᎩᏴ” ᏙᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏯᏂᏪᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Really, I’ve heard them saying that. And I’ve heard the elders: “ They’re going to be building houses where they can’t be built. Anywhere you go, around, just anywhere in the mountains, beautiful houses will be there. It wasn’t like that long ago.” That’s what they really used to say.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: “Everywhere, there will be houses,” they said.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᎴ “ᎥᏳᎦ ᏅᎾᏛᏂ ᎠᎯᎵᏙᎮᏍᏗ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏁᎲᎾ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎨᏍᏗ--ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎨᏕ ᎠᏆᏛᎦᏅ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ “ᏞᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏓᏗᏴᎵᏛᏍᎩ ᏲᎩᎮ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎣᎩᎩᏌ ᏃᏭᏛᏃ ᏃᏛ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏲᎬ ᎤᏁᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᏃᏭᏛ ᏥᏬᏧᏓᎴᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ ᏦᏣᎴᏂᏍᎬ ᏦᏥᎧᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᏍᎩᎶ ᎠᏝ Ꮓ ᏙᎬᏓᎡᎬ ᏱᏬᏣᎴᏂ ᎨᎲ. ᎩᎳ Ꮓ ᎣᏍᏓᏃ ᏳᏴᏢᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏗᏓᏴᎵᏛᏍᎦ ᏃᎴ ᏥᏬᏣᎦᏙᏍᏗᎰ ᎣᎦᏅᏛ ᎮᏂ Mama general hospital ᏱᏚᎦᏙᏍᏛᏂ ‘Ꭽ! ᏃᎴ Ꮫ Mama general hospital ᏓᎦᏙᏍᏓ!’ ᎣᎩᏲᏤᎲ Ꮎ T.V. ᎤᏁᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓᏃᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏳᏴᏝᏓ ᏃᎴᏛ ᏥᏓᎠᏨᏥᎯᎲ ᎠᏝᏅ ᏙᎦᏓᎡᎦ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ”
segments.translation: Then, “A virus they don’t know about will be going around, and they won’t have any medicine for it,” they will be saying--I mean, they would say. I’ve heard them talking, “We didn’t have television. Then, when we got one, it would go out. When it turned all white, we would unplug it, then we would move tables or chairs and toss rubber rings. [laughter] Until the T.V. cooled down, then we’d start watching again. We would watch General Hospital. [laughter] “Haw! Mama’s watching General Hospital, again.” She was causing it to break down on us - it would just get white. Then when it cooled down good, it would come back on. We would play rubber ring toss [game] ’til then.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏙᏳ ᏧᏂᏰᎸᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎡᎵᏌ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏥᏚᎦᏙᏍᏛ ᏓᏁᎸ ᏥᏭᎷᏨ. “ᎤᏫ!” ᏣᏗᎲᏛ ᏥᎦᏃᎮᏍᎬ “Leslie Ꮕ ᎠᏲᎱ” ᏥᎦᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬᏛ
segments.translation: Some really thought that was something. My grandma, she watched it all the time. She came to our house. “Ooh-wee!” she said. “Leslie died,” she said.
They thought it was real.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: My dad said, “Who was that?”
My mom and them thought it was real.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏣᏅᏘᏃ Ꮎ “ᎾᎾ Ꮎ General Hospital” -- “Ꭽ!” ᏧᏛᏅ Dad - ᎡᏙᏓ “ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏒ ᏙᏳ ᎩᎶ ᎡᏥᏃᎮᏍᎬ!” ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: “Haw!” he said, “I thought you were talking about a real person.”

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏓᏌᏓ ᎮᎢ “Ꭽ!” ᏅᏛᏅ “ᏗᎾᏓᏲᏁ” ᏯᏗᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏱᏫᎦᏅᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ, “ᎤᏂᎯᏐᏙᏭ ᏗᎾᏓᏲᏁᎭ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏱᎦ ᏥᏕᏣᎦᏙᏍᏗ” ᏯᎪᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: That Da-sa-d(a)! “Haw! That’s them marriage breakers,” he’d say. [laughter] He would go out, “It’s lonely, them marriage breakers, that’s all you’re watching,” he’d say to Mom.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏳᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏱᎦ ᏥᏚᏅᎦᏙᏍᏛ ᏙᎭ? ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮫ ᏣᏩᏅᏛ ᎭᎳᎩ ᎠᏟᎩᎵᏎ Ꮎ ᏚᎦᏙᏍᏛ
segments.translation: Really, that’s all they watched, didn’t they? When she watched it, that’s when I knew what time it was.
Two [o’clock].

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Two [o’clock].
[laughter]

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎠᏯ Ꮓ ᏣᎩᏍᏗᎬ. ᎾᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᏦᏥᏁᎸ ᎾᎮᏂ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎾᏅ ᎣᎩᏒᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎦᏅᎯᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏝ ᏥᏕᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏝ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏳᏬᏟ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ Mama ᏱᎦᏰᏫᏒᏍᎩ ᏱᏗᎦᏁᎶᏂᏙ Ꮒ barnabas Ꭲ Barnabas Ꭲ ᏳᏛᏂᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᎦᏕᏢᏍᏗᎲ ᎦᏂᏝ ᏥᏫᎦᏓᏕᎡᎬ ᏥᏫᏥᎸᏍᎬ ᏥᏍᎦᎢᎲᎾ Barnabas
segments.translation: Myself, where we lived when I was little, the kitchen and where we slept was all a real long room. And on this side [gestures], there were rooms in front. There Mama would sit at the table, sewing, and I would be playing. “Ni Barnabas! Ni Barnabas!” she’d say. I’d run past where she was sitting, dive onto the bed and go to sleep. [laughter] I was afraid of Barnabas.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I remember that!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Used to be on “Dark Shadows.” Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏦᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏃᎮᏂ Ꮓ ᎤᎴᎾᏗ ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᏂᏙᎲ Ꮓ “Barnabas Ꭲ! Barnabas Ꭲ!” ᏳᏛᎾᏃ ᏥᎦᏗᏢᏍᏗᎲ Ꮓ ᎦᏀᎯᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏝ ᎠᏰᏟᏃ ᎣᎩᏍᎩᎸ ᎣᎦᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎣᎩᏒᏍᏗ ᏭᎵᏍᏛᏴ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎾᏛ ᏱᎦᎵᏢᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮪ Ꮪ Ꮪ Ꮪ! ᎦᏂᏝ ᏱᏩᏓᏓᎤᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, it was three o’clock, it was time for her to start cooking I think. I was playing around, and then, “It’s Barnabas! It’s Barnabas!” she’d say. And I’d run by. It was real long, that room. Where she cooked was on this side [gestures]. In the middle of it, we had a table where we ate. Then where we slept was at the end. I’d run by there, and I’d dive onto the bed.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎦᎾᏰᎩ Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏚᏂᏃᎩᏍᏛ ᏣᎾᏗ
segments.translation: He was scary like that. And you know, the songs they sang.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: I was scared of him.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Barnabas Collins, it was.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I think you can still watch that.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: They say you can. I don’t really know.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎩᎶ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ “ᏴᎦᏙᏍᏓ Ꮟ” ᏣᎾᏗᎲ. “ᏝᏲ ᎠᏯ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ” ᏥᎦᏥᏲᎮᎥ
segments.translation: Someone said that. “You can still watch it,” -- “But I don’t want to,” I said.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Me neither.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎦᏂᏰᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ. “ᎤᏓᏅᏘᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ Barnabas” ᏯᎾᏗ ᎤᏓᏅᏘᏍ ᎨᎮ?
segments.translation: He was scary. “Barnabas was friendly,” they’ll say. Was he friendly?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: I don’t know. I just saw him.
My late mom used to watch it, but not me.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏭ ᏳᏂᎧᎭ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᏭ ᏂᎦ “Barnabas, Barnabas” ᏃᎴ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏏᏆ ᏥᏕᏥᏍᎦᏱᎲ ... ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᏂ ᏥᏥᏃᏍᎩᏍᎪ ᏥᏥᏅᎪᎪ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏥᏈᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏍGᏊ ᏪᏌ ᏥᏕᎯᎾᏝᎥ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᎩᏅᏅ ᎦᎳᏅᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏥᏄᏅᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᏧᏂ- ᏧᏂ- Ꮩ ᏴᏗ? Ꮎ ᏧᏂ--
segments.translation: They would be right there. “Barnabas, Barnabas.” Then, too, I was afraid of hogs. Sometimes I would sneak out of the house. I had a lot of cats, then. And they made the thing real high… The…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They had a nest?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: They made the latch, so I couldn’t get out.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, they had it locked.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏍᎩᏅ ᎦᏍᎩᎶᏭᏅ ᎩᎶᏫᏴ ᏳᏩᏯ ᎨᎲ ᏳᏩᏍᏚᎢ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᎬᏬᏎᎲ. ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏴᏫ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ Ꮕ ᎬᎩᏘᎾᏫᏗᎮ ᎸᏢᏅ ᎤᏯᏅ ᎤᏂᏏᎳᏛ ᎤᎾᏅ ᎠᏮᏛᏤᎴ ᎠᏩᏌᏃ ᎤᎾᏭᏅ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᏁ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎡᏥ Ꮕ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏪᏌ ᏚᏍᏓᏩᏛᏎ ᏌᏭ Ꮕ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏝ ᏳᏬᏟ ᎨᎮ ᏐᎢᎾ ᏭᏟᏴ ᎤᎾᏅᏅ ᎬᏩᏘᏁᎨ Mama Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏂᏎᎮ ᎤᎾ ᏗᎨᏙᎲ. ᎤᎾᏅ ᎠᏩᏛᏤᎴ ᎠᏩᏒᏃ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎤᏂᏄᎸᏁᏅ ᎬᎩᏘᎾᏫᏗᎲ Ꮎ
segments.translation: “She would get that chair and open the door.” They talked about me one time. They were saying the little people were taking me somewhere. They had fence wire up, and my dress got hung up there. I couldn’t get free. Then, my mom, she followed the cats. One would be sitting on one side and the other on the other side. They were trying to lead Momma. Telling her where I was, my dress got hung up there. She said they couldn’t take me…

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: ’Cause you got hung up.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: …to their bluff.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎤᎥ, well ᎰᏩ ᎢᏗᏍᏆᏗᏗᎾ ᏛᎾ ᏌᏭᏃ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏛᎬᏯᏛᏛᏂ. ᎾᎾ ᎯᎢ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏥᏗᏬᏂ ᏛᎵᏒᏂᏍ ᎮᎵ ᏩᎦᏛᏭ Ꭸ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: Well, OK, we’re getting done. Now, I’m going to ask you one thing. This Cherokee we’re speaking, is it going to run out or keep going?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎡᎵᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏓᎾᏛᏍᎩ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎢᎦᏕ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏛᎾᏝᏂᎬᏁᎵ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏙᏛᎾᏓᏲᏏ. ᏙᏛᎾᏓᏲᏏ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏂᏛᏳᏅᏛᏁᎵ Ꮎ ᎠᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᎤᎾᏕᎳᏆᎥ ᎴᏱᎦ. ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏱᏚᏂᎧᎯ ᏴᏫ ᏧᏂᏅᏫᏍᏗᏍᎦ. ᏢᏅ ᎰᏩᏅ ᏯᏁᎰ ᏍᎫ ᏂᎦ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗᏭ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎬᎩᏛᏛᏅ ᏯᏁᎯ ᎮᏂ ᏴᏫ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎦ “ᏲᎦᏚᎳ ᏧᏂᏍᏕᎸᏗᎯ ᏣᎾᏕᎳᏆ” ᏥᎦᏥᏃᏎᎸᏂ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏱᏧᎾᏛᏁ
segments.translation: Maybe these kids growing up, some of them might put in the effort, but some are going to give up. Something else is going to get in the way of what they learn or have learned. And, if they have people to coach them there, not that many are around. All there is, is the school. One time they asked me if there were any fluent Cherokee speakers around. “We’d like them to help these students,” I told them that, but they didn’t say anything.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎢᎦᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏓᎾᏕᎳᏆ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ
segments.translation: Those kids are really learning good.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏓ ᎾᏂ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏳᏂᏬᏂᏎ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏳᏂᎷᏤ boy ᏍᎦᏎᏗ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᎢᎦᏓ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏟᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏯᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᎪ
segments.translation: Some of them never spoke any Cherokee until they came here. Now, they speak really good, and some are not learning a lot.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏎᎾ ᎾᏛ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᎩᎶᏫ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᎠᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᎪ
segments.translation: But the little ones, they’re learning real quick.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏗᎨᏥᏍᏗᏰᏛᏅ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏓᏳᏂᏄᎸᏂ ᎤᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ
segments.translation: Some, too, probably been pressured into learning it, they might struggle to learn it because of that.
If they don’t want to learn themselves.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Their own, and from their hearts they wanted.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: From their hearts, right.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᎩᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏱᎪᎯᏳ ᎩᎳ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏓᎦᎵᏍᏛᏂ
segments.translation: Until it’s in our hearts, and we believe, then it will happen.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Right.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Right.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏄᏍᏗ Ꭰ yeah Ꭰ ᎠᏯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᎦ ᏗᏩᏛᏒ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᎬᏛᎦᏁᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎢᎦ ᎨᎩᏬᏛ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎢᎦ ᏣᎨᏳᎯ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏣᏁᎸ ᎤᏁᎳᏅᎯ Ꮲ ᏯᎾᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᏴᏫ ᏃᏭ ᏍᎫ ᏥᎦ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏛᏅᏍᎬ ᏳᎾᏚᎸᏓ ᏳᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏯᎾᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᏝᎩ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᎡᏓᏕᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎡᎶᎯ
segments.translation: That’s the way it is, but myself, as I was growing up, the way I’ve heard, the way they preached to us, love what has been given to you from God, people don’t think about that today. Now something happens because they want it. They don’t think about how long we’re here on Earth.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah, really.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎬᏩᎩᏗ Ꮓ ᎩᎾᏂᎩᏐᎲᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎡᎶᎯ ᎬᏩᎦᏗ ᎮᏃ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏙᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏳᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏩᏟᎶᎮᎸ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏅᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎤᏟᏗᏢ ᏧᏬᏢ ᎤᏁᎳᏅᎯ ᏫᎯᎷᏨ ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏓ ᏓᎧᏁᏥᏍ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎢᎨ ᎲᎥ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏣᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᏴ ᏭᎵᏍᏗ ᎤᎵᏍᎨᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏩᏛᏏᏏᏒ ᎬᏪᏲᏅ ᎬᎩᏬᎾᏛᏅ ᏍᎫᏍᎫ ᎤᏠᏯ ᏕᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏱᏣᏍᏆᎶᎨᏍᏗ ᏧᏏᏭ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏧᏌ ᏨᏓᏛ ᏂᏓᏳᏓᎴᏅᏗ ᏣᏕᎵᏆᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᎬᏃᏎ ᏱᎦ ᎤᎵᏍᎨᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏁᎸ ᎤᏁᎳᏅᎯ and ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᎾᏕᎳᎰᏏ ᏳᎾᏓᏅᏖᏟ ᎠᏯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᎦ ᎢᎦᏓᎦᏴᎵᎦ ᎩᏅᏂᏒᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎾᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬᏂ ᎨᎲ but ᎠᏎᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ
segments.translation: Forever, we’ll be gone from Earth forever. Really, we have to work at it, until it can be good. When the time comes that you’re not around, and you go before God, how you going to speak, English? No, what he has given you, that much is sacred. They taught me as I was growing up, and preached to me the same thing I’m telling my kids: if you come up short, it’s on you. You have to learn from your own heart, and I’m telling you how sacred is what was given to you by God. That, if they realize and think about it, us the parents, it is our fault they’re not learning it, but when they go to school…

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: When they went there, yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏳᏂᏲᎱᏌ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎨ ᏴᏓ you got to give them a fighting chance
segments.translation: That’s where they lose it, but, how would you say, we give them a fighting chance.

segments.text: I had that Tommy Smith (…) ᎤᎾ ᎪᎢ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎦ
segments.translation: I had that Tommy Smith (…) There at Greasy. He spoke well.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Tommy, Tommy!
He spoke well.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Is he still living?

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.text: ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗᏓ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏕᏥᏰᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎦᏬᏂᎲ then ᏃᏭᏅ ᎣᎩᏂᏍᏆᏗᏕᏂ Ꮓ ᎦᏳᎵ Ꮭ ᏳᏚᎵᎮ “Red, red. I like red” – “ᏓᏥᏃᏎᎳ ᏣᏙᏓ ᏓᏨᎸᏂᎳ” – “Ꮭ!” – “ᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏚᎵ ᏣᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ” – “ᎤᏁᎩᏟᏗᏭ ᏂᏩ” ... It’s up too ᏥᏂᏗᏪ ᎤᏅᏏ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏚᏟᏗ
segments.translation: Yeah, he’s raising a little girl. And I was teaching her Cherokee. She was speaking it good. As we were about done, then she didn’t want to. “Red, I like Red!” [laughter] “I’m going to tell your dad, and he’s going to whip you!” – “No!” -- “He wants you to learn Cherokee!” – “That’s ugly, what you’re saying!” Like we were saying, they got to want to on their own.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Sue Ann Ꮕ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎭ Tommy ᏣᏗ
segments.translation: Sue Ann was married to him, wasn’t it, I think, who you’re saying - Tommy.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah, Tommy.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: So, he’s raising the girl?

segments.text: Yes, ᎦᎵᏍᏆᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏗ ᏳᏕᏘᏳᏓ Tommy ᎯᏍᎩ ᏑᏓᎵ ᎴᏱᎦ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏚᎾᏟᏴ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ
segments.translation: Tommy is over 70 years old. I think the girl is five or six, all the time they get into it, with her elder.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ Lorretta ᎨᎵ ᎤᎾᏝᏩᏍᏗ ᎤᎾ Ꮎ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏧᎪᏁᎸ Ꮎ Lorretta Sumpter ᏥᏓᏳᎪᏁᎸ BunchᎢ
segments.translation: I think Loretta stays with them too, after her house burned down.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: That’s what they said.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏄᏛᏅᏕᎬ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏧᏥᎦᏘᎲ ᏥᏥᏍᏕᎸᎡᎲ ᏑᏓᏁᎸᏫ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ “ᏥᏩᎩᏑᎸᎪᏨ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏗᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᎤᏪᏣ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᏛᏁᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᏩᎾᏘ ᎮᏂ ᎯᎨᏳᏒ” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎵ “ᎠᏎᎾ ᏂᏛᎬᏪᏎᎳ Ꮎ ᏧᏪᏙ ᏥᏍᏕᎸᎡᎰ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏱᏓᏤᏟᏭ ᏱᏣᏑᎵᎪᏥ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏛᏌᏛᏂ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎤᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ” ᏥᏈᏍᏙᎲᏅ ᎤᎾ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎵ ᎫᏍᏓ ᏳᏩᎾᏙᏗ ᏗᎦᏚᎴᏂ ᏱᎦ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᎬᏁᎲ “ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏛᏒᏛᏂ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎤᏃᏍᎩᏍᏗ” ᏧᏛᏅ “ᎮᏍᏗᏭ ᏳᏪᏙᎮᏍᏗ ᎲᏍᎫ ᏱᎦᏣᏅᏘ ᎤᏂᏁᎫᏥᏓ ᏳᏩᎬᏩᏃᎵᎦ ᏂᎯᏅ ᎠᏰᏟ ᏳᏫᏣᏑᏱ” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎤᎵᏍᏆᏟᏗ ᎬᏪᏙᎶ Ꮓ ᏥᏭᏁᎸ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎾᏃ Tommy Ꭲ ᏥᏭᏓᏝᏩᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᏎᎾ Ᏺ ᏧᏂᎨᏳᏛᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏭᏕᏗ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏛᏁᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎮᏂ ᎢᎦ ᎮᏂ

segments.translation: Has he been here, that Tommy?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I don’t think he has, no.
We’ll have to tell him.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏰᏗ ᎡᎵᏍᏗ ᏙᎭ Tommy
segments.translation: Really, that Tommy, he can come, you’d think.
What about Janice? Has she come by? She’s crazy.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: She’s funny, ain’t it?
Yeah, she is funny. Haw.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏫ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᏙᎩ ᏥᏓᏗ ᎪᎯ ᏇᏗ
segments.translation: She works close by, what did we say? Gwe-d(i).

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Oh, Kelly.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Kelly works here.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.text: ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏗᎾᏝᏃᎮᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ Ꮎ ᏏᎮᏂ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏂᏥᏪᏍᎬ Ꮓ ᎠᏂᎬᏴᎵ ᏱᏚᏂᏲᎱᏌ Ꮓ ᏚᎾᏓᏘᏅᏅ ᏫᏓᎾᎵᏍᎩᎵᏰᏍᎪ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎤᏂᏍᏛᏗᎲ ᎤᏂᎨᏳᎲᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᎦᏗ ᏢᏅ ᎠᏓᎨᏗ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: But I don’t know if they talk to each other. That’s what I was saying, the elders pass on, they separate the kids, something they get into over, being stingy with things, that’s what I’m saying. There’s no love for one another, that’s not love.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Yeah, ᎦᏕᎳᎣᏍᎩᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏗᏓ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏝ ᏑᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ Ꮲ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᏗᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏗ ᏱᎦ
segments.translation: Yeah, I can see that, that’s the way it’s going with families, but it’s none of my business on that, just let them be doing that.

segments.speaker: marlene-glass
segments.translation: Yeah. Just let them be, I think.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Well, ᎰᏩ ᎢᏗᏍᏆᏗᏛ ᏙᏲ ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ ᏥᏍᏕᏗ Marlene, ᏙᏳ ᎪᎯᏗ ᎦᎬᎪᎥ
segments.translation: OK, we’re done, I’m thankful both of you came. Marlene, it has been a very long time since I’ve seen you.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Me too, I’m really thankful.
